THE EVIDENCE™

Can You Be a Democrat and a Christian? Put All Ten Commandments on the Table.

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best-Selling Author
The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

I keep hearing a line that ought to make any Christian stop and think. “Well, the God I serve would never do that.” Sometimes it comes from someone wrestling honestly with Scripture. Sometimes it comes before the person has even opened the Bible. They already know what God has to think, because He has to agree with them.

That gets us to a question I’ve wanted to ask Christian Democrats directly. When the party says one thing and Scripture says another, which one are you willing to correct?

I’ve heard the charge that the left routinely breaks most, if not all, of the Ten Commandments. There are ten, so let’s go through all ten. We’ll look at what was said in Congress, what lawmakers voted to take, what a jury found, and what people told a pollster they would feel if the president were murdered. Where I’m giving you my own experience or my reading of Scripture, I’ll say so.

1. Thou shalt have no other gods before me

I suspect a fair number of people who call themselves Christian mean they grew up Christian, celebrate Christmas, and think of themselves as decent people. That’s what I mean by cultural Christian. I want to know what authority Christ has in their lives when following Him costs them something.

How far can I take that charge against Democrats? Pew’s 2023–24 Religious Landscape Study found that about four in ten Democrats and Democratic leaners were religiously unaffiliated, a category that includes atheists, agnostics, and people who say their religion is “nothing in particular.” Thirty-five percent said they prayed daily, and 24 percent said they attended religious services at least monthly. Among Black Democrats, 75 percent said they believed in God or a universal spirit with absolute certainty. Those results show substantial differences within the party. A survey can count religious habits and professions of belief. Christ knows what those professions mean.

Then there’s the person who acts as if he answers to nobody. Acts 12 tells of a crowd acclaiming Herod’s voice as the voice of a god. Herod accepted the glory. That passage comes to mind when I hear people in power speak as though their office gives them the authority to settle every moral question for everyone else. I can judge what an official claims the right to do. Whether he thinks himself godlike is a question about his heart.

2. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image

“The God I serve would never do that.” All right. How did you come to know that about Him?

If you can show me the Scripture, let’s read it. I may have overlooked something. But if you start with the answer you want and cut away every passage that challenges it, what exactly are you worshiping? The finished product may bear the name of God and have every opinion its maker started with.

Exodus speaks of making an image and bowing down to it. My application is that a person can also make an idol out of an idea of God. You can do it without carving a single piece of wood. Take the parts of Jesus you find agreeable, edit out the parts that call you to repent, and put what’s left to work endorsing your politics. If the god you serve has never told you anything you didn’t want to hear, I’d ask who made him.

3. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain

When I get an “F-you” on X over a political post, my first guess is that it came from the left. That’s based on the replies I’ve received. I can tell you what my feed looks like. Ranking the left against every political movement in history would require evidence I don’t have.

Ordinary profanity and taking God’s name in vain are distinct biblical questions. Ephesians 4:29 addresses corrupt speech. Exodus 20 addresses the use of God’s name. I have a problem with both the contempt people sling at strangers and the willingness of some politicians to enlist Jesus in a campaign.

In 2022, California Governor Gavin Newsom’s reelection campaign put up billboards advertising abortion access in states that restricted it. One version quoted Jesus’ command to love your neighbor. Newsom said California wanted women to know it would help them. Fine. Then answer the question your own billboard invites. Does the unborn child count as a neighbor? If you’re going to put Jesus’ words on the billboard, you ought to be willing to answer for everyone affected by the policy you’re selling.

4. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy

Nevada Democrats began their 2016 presidential caucuses at 11 a.m. on a Saturday. Voters had to attend in person. That put observant Jews and Seventh-day Adventists who keep the Saturday Sabbath in a bind. Nevada Republicans had also caucused on a Saturday in 2012 and arranged an alternate time after sundown. An accommodation was possible. The Democrats’ scheduling decision gives us a specific instance in which they could have made room for religious observance and failed to do so.

Christians differ on how they observe the Sabbath. The question here is practical. When you know some voters have set that time aside for God, and you control when the caucus takes place, how hard is it to give them another time to participate?

5. Honour thy father and thy mother

The commandment addresses children. It should also prompt adults in government to ask whether they respect the responsibilities that come with being a father or a mother.

In Montgomery County, Maryland, the school board introduced elementary-school storybooks dealing with sexuality and gender. It initially notified parents and let them excuse their children from instruction involving those books. Then it withdrew the accommodation. In 2025, the Supreme Court held that the parents who brought the case were entitled to a preliminary injunction. The families came from several religious traditions. The decision addressed their free-exercise rights in that case.

The example is a local school board’s decision. The political question I’d put to anyone who defended it is straightforward. You had a way to teach the lesson and let objecting parents excuse their children. What became so important about making those particular children sit through it?

6. Thou shalt not kill

The Democratic Party’s 2024 national platform called for restoring Roe v. Wade protections through federal law, repealing the Hyde Amendment’s restrictions on federal abortion funding, and continuing to support access to medication abortion. Democrats argue that restrictions endanger women’s health and interfere with decisions women should be free to make. I believe the unborn child is a human life we’re responsible for protecting. I also believe a woman facing a dangerous pregnancy deserves prompt medical care. If a Christian Democrat shares those convictions, I’d like to know what protection for unborn children that person has been willing to demand from the party.

Now consider what people are willing to say about the murder of a political opponent. In September 2026, reporting on a Center for Strategic Politics survey said 23 percent of the Democrats surveyed would feel “very positive” if President Trump were assassinated while speaking at a rally. Another 9 percent said “somewhat positive.” That question measured a stated reaction to one hypothetical assassination. The figures apply to the Democrats surveyed and the scenario named in the question. I found no basis in that question for extending the figure to the vice president, Cabinet, or anyone else in the administration.

The question as asked is ugly enough. These respondents were offered the prospect of a man being murdered, and they described how good it would make them feel. A Christian is commanded to love his enemies. What do we say in church about taking pleasure in an enemy’s murder when the man in the question is someone we spent the week denouncing?

7. Thou shalt not commit adultery

In August 1998, President Bill Clinton acknowledged his relationship with Monica Lewinsky while he was married. He said he had misled people, including his wife. His own address gives us a specific case involving a Democratic president. It tells us what he admitted, and it leaves his defenders to answer for what they were willing to excuse.

People can forgive a man and still say he broke his vows. The test for Christians in politics is whether they’ll say that plainly while the man is useful to them. I’d ask the same of a Republican defending a Republican president.

8. Thou shalt not steal

Start in New Orleans. Former Mayor Ray Nagin was convicted of offenses including bribery, wire fraud, and money laundering and was sentenced to ten years in federal prison in 2014. The case involved people doing business with the city. It shows how a public official can put the power of his office to work for private gain and then move the proceeds through transactions that help conceal where they came from.

Then look at former Democratic Senator Bob Menendez. A jury convicted him in 2024, and he was sentenced to 11 years in prison in January 2025 for offenses including bribery and obstruction. The Justice Department documented cash and gold bars. It also described how bribe money returned by Menendez and his wife was falsely characterized as loan repayments in documents produced to a grand jury. The bribery case shows what people were prepared to pay for access to public power. The false loan story shows the work that went into concealing the payments.

When I look at a money-laundering case, I want to know where the money came from, who benefited, and what was done to disguise it. The record in each case has to carry the charge. Nagin’s money-laundering conviction and Menendez’s bribery and obstruction convictions give us two concrete cases to examine.

9. Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour

On September 26, 2019, House Intelligence Committee Chairman Adam Schiff opened a public hearing with an imagined version of President Trump’s July 25 call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Schiff introduced it as his rendering of the call’s essence and then spoke in Trump’s voice. He had Trump say he wanted Zelenskyy to “make up dirt on my political opponent.” Later in the hearing, Schiff said his summary was meant at least partly as parody.

Read the released White House memorandum. It expressly says it is a record of the call rather than a verbatim transcript. It records Trump asking about the Bidens and asking Zelenskyy to look into the matter. That was real and fair to scrutinize. Schiff’s instruction to make up damaging material is absent from the memo. Those two words turn a request to investigate into a request to fabricate. That is a serious difference, especially when you’re the chairman opening an official hearing. Congress had the actual memorandum it could quote. Why give the public an invented line in the president’s voice?

Then there’s the falsehood that gets repeated. On May 8, 2024, President Joe Biden said inflation was 9 percent when he took office. On May 14, he said it again. The Bureau of Labor Statistics put annual inflation at 1.4 percent in January 2021, when he took office. That’s a readily verifiable figure, and the false claim made the economy Biden inherited look worse. Voters heard it twice in six days. They deserved a correction as public as the claim.

These examples show how falsehood can enter ordinary political business. One was delivered at the opening of a congressional hearing. Another was repeated in presidential interviews. The Menendez case goes further, with a false account placed in documents produced to a grand jury. Each example can be tested against the record. That’s where I’d start if a party leader told me their side takes truth seriously.

10. Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s goods

Here in Washington, the Legislature enacted a 9.9 percent state income tax scheduled to begin January 1, 2028. The Department of Revenue says it applies above $1 million in annual adjusted gross income, with a $1 million threshold for a married couple filing jointly. The rate applies to the taxable amount above the threshold. Washington lawmakers now have a particular group of neighbors in mind when they tell us who should pay more.

At the federal level, the Democrats’ 2024 platform called for a 25 percent minimum income tax on billionaires. In March 2026, Senator Elizabeth Warren and other Democrats introduced a separate proposal to tax wealth itself. Their bill would impose an annual 2 percent tax on taxable net assets above $50 million through $1 billion, with a higher rate on assets above $1 billion. That tax could come due even in a year when the owner sold nothing. Washington’s law and Warren’s bill reach different things. One reaches annual income. The other reaches assets already owned.

Where does Marx come in? Marx and Engels expressly called for a steeply graduated income tax in The Communist Manifesto, alongside proposals that went considerably further, including abolishing private ownership of land. The parallel I see is the political appeal of identifying a class of people by what they own and making their property the answer to other people’s demands. A graduated tax rate alone tells me little about a lawmaker’s ideology. How lawmakers sell the taking, what limits they accept, and what they intend to do with the proceeds tell me more.

Romans 13 recognizes an obligation to pay taxes. Supporters of higher taxes on the wealthy argue that those who can afford more should pay more toward public needs. They can make that argument by naming the need, showing what it costs, and defending who ought to pay. I’m asking what happens when the appeal boils down to “Look what he has. He has too much. Vote for us and we’ll take some of it.” I call that an appeal to covetousness. The commandment says thy neighbour’s goods. Your neighbor still counts when he makes a million dollars.

Can you be a Democrat and a Christian at the same time?

Yes. What I want to know is which one gets to tell the other no.

If you believe life in the womb deserves protection, tell your Democratic candidate what protection you expect him to vote for. If you know your president gave the public a false number twice, demand a correction. If a congressional chairman puts invented words in another man’s mouth, call it out while he’s still on your side. If your party wants a new tax, ask it to justify the public need without asking you to resent the people who will pay it. And if someone says it would make them happy to see the president murdered, tell them what Christ said about loving your enemies.

The same test applies to me and to anyone whose preferred candidate gives him something to gain by overlooking what he knows. Where has your faith cost you something with your own side? I offered Kendall Hubbard three nicknames and asked her to pick one. She gave me a little smile and said, “I could just claim all of them.” Somewhere in Oxford, a Miami equipment manager is looking at the back of a volleyball jersey and wondering how small the letters can go.

The Dime Dealer has 2,644 career assists to her name. The Maestro ran the Mount Notre Dame offense and captained the Cougars for two years. And if you have questions about the Kill Switch, Anthony Wayne had a pretty good view of her 10 kills in the regional semifinal. Throw in 41 assists and 18 digs that same night, and I’m the guy who asked a setter with a triple-double to choose ONE of anything.

I’d followed Kendall online before I saw her play. The first time was Senior Night at Bishop Fenwick, in a gym that made it plenty clear whose seniors they were celebrating. The second was that five-setter against the Generals at Vandalia Butler. MND lost both, and I like to give players their space after a loss. Funny thing is, by the time I finally met Kendall, I already knew her voice.

At Butler I was on the floor at center court, taking pictures five to ten feet from her. When I thought the match was slipping away, I could hear Kendall encouraging her teammates. They pushed Anthony Wayne to 22–20 in the fifth. Best match I saw all season. I was heartbroken for the Cougars, and I’ll always appreciate the Generals’ captains for making a point of telling me afterward, on camera and off, how good Kendall was. I still wonder how far that MND team could’ve gone.

She made the state semifinals as a junior and earned Division II first-team All-Ohio and District 16 Player of the Year as a senior. When we finally met at Lakota East and I asked about MND, what she wanted to talk about was practice with her teammates. “It’s my favorite part of the day.” That’s when she grew another ten feet in my eyes.

Congratulations, Kendall. Take all three nicknames to Miami. I’ll bring my camera. Somebody else can push that cart.

text:
THE EVIDENCE™

THE TRADE SEATTLE NEVER MADE

The Seahawks had a way to trade Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. Why did they let him reach free agency?

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best-Selling Author
November 20, 2026
The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.
On February 8, Kenneth Walker III ran for 135 yards in Seattle’s 29–13 Super Bowl LX victory over New England. He became the first running back since Terrell Davis to win the game’s MVP award. On March 3, the Seahawks let the franchise-tag deadline pass. A month after the Super Bowl, Walker was a Kansas City Chief. Seattle’s projected return is a fifth-round compensatory pick in 2027.

Here’s what makes the decision worth examining. John Schneider had already tagged a player and traded him to Kansas City. Seattle did it with defensive end Frank Clark in 2019. Seven years later, the same general manager let the Super Bowl MVP reach the open market. What made Walker’s case different?

Walker had a reason to wait

Seattle could have negotiated a contract with Walker and arranged a trade. That required his signature and a team willing to pay him and send Seattle compensation. Walker told Mike Florio in May that he had come to expect during the 2025 season that he would be leaving. By the time free agency opened, he figured his time in Seattle was over.

Put yourself in Walker’s shoes. If Kansas City wants you, why sign a contract that makes Kansas City give up a draft pick to get you? He could weigh offers in free agency and choose his destination. Seattle would have needed to give him a reason to sign first, and a buyer would have needed a reason to pay for a player it might soon be able to sign directly.

Kansas City gave Walker a three-year deal with a base value of $43.05 million, including $28.7 million fully guaranteed. The Chiefs paid an average of $14.35 million per year and kept their draft picks. That establishes what Kansas City was willing to pay Walker. The public record leaves open what the Chiefs, or anyone else, would have offered Seattle for him.

The $14.3 million decision

The nonexclusive franchise tag for a running back was $14.293 million. Seattle could have used it to retain the right to match an outside offer. If another club signed Walker to an offer sheet and Seattle declined to match, the standard compensation would have been two first-round picks. A negotiated trade could have fetched a different price, but Walker would first have needed to sign a contract. The cheaper $11.323 million transition tag offered matching rights without draft compensation if Seattle declined to match.

The franchise tender would have counted against Seattle’s cap while it looked for a buyer. If Walker signed it and a trade fell through, Seattle could have been left with the one-year salary commitment. That was the wager. How much of a draft-pick upgrade would justify tying up that cap room, and who was prepared to offer it?

Green Bay found a buyer for Davante Adams in 2022. The Raiders gave up a first and a second and agreed to a new contract with Adams. Seattle itself had used the franchise tag twice under Schneider, on kicker Olindo Mare in 2010 and on Clark in 2019. Those deals establish that the mechanism works when a buyer meets the price. Adams, a two-time first-team All-Pro receiver at the time of the trade, gives us precedent for the transaction. Walker’s market would have set its own price.

What Seattle got by waiting

https://t.co/eJS8sM1r9f, using Over the Cap data, projects a fourth-round compensatory pick for Boye Mafe and fifth-rounders for Walker, Coby Bryant and Riq Woolen. The league will determine the awards after the season. Trading Walker would have taken his departure out of the free-agent formula, so a trade offer had to be weighed against the pick Seattle expected by letting him leave.

Seattle was already making decisions with those projected picks in mind. In April, Schneider sent Cleveland a 2027 fourth-rounder for the fifth-round pick he used on Iowa guard Beau Stephens. Afterward, Schneider said the club had a plan to use the compensatory system. That puts Walker’s projected fifth-rounder in context. Seattle was counting on several extra selections and had already used that expected depth to justify spending a future pick.

The Seahawks also committed three years and $51 million to receiver and returner Rashid Shaheed. That’s $2.65 million more per year on average than Walker’s Chiefs deal, but the annual averages hide the immediate cap trade-off. Over the Cap lists Shaheed’s 2026 charge at $7 million, roughly half the one-year Walker tag. Seattle signed Emanuel Wilson and used a first-round pick on Jadarian Price. Schneider’s public assessment was blunt. He called Walker “outstanding” and said running back was a position where Seattle could find players.

What the field has shown

Through Week 10, Walker had 872 rushing yards, seven rushing touchdowns and four receiving touchdowns for Kansas City. He entered the Atlanta weekend eight rushing yards behind league leader Bijan Robinson and missed the November 15 game with a groin injury. The Chiefs paid for a lead back, and for most of the first ten weeks, they got one.

Seattle saw both sides of its decision in consecutive games. On October 25 at Lumen Field, the Seahawks held Walker to 36 yards on 14 carries and beat Kansas City 20–3. Wilson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries. The following week, Price returned from a chest injury and Zach Charbonnet played his first game since tearing his ACL in January. They combined for 52 yards on 16 carries in a 34–17 loss to Chicago. Seattle got a strong night out of Wilson against the Chiefs. The next game showed how quickly the backfield question could reopen.

My Findings

Seattle had a way to create trade leverage, and it chose to let the deadline pass. Schneider had used that leverage before with Frank Clark. With Walker, he preserved cap flexibility and went into the offseason expecting a compensatory pick. The unanswered question is whether Seattle had a buyer willing to beat that projected return by enough to justify the tag. A documented offer would tell us more about the decision than any comparison to Davante Adams.

Replacing Walker took real resources. Seattle signed Wilson and spent a first-round pick on Price while Charbonnet recovered. The front office’s premise is that it can find enough production at running back while paying veterans at other positions. Beating Kansas City showed how well that approach can work on a given Sunday. Walker’s production over ten weeks shows the caliber of player Seattle had to replace.

In January, we’ll have a fuller record of what Seattle got from its backfield. In the spring, we’ll know what the league actually awards for Walker’s departure. Until then, the clearest fact is this. Kansas City has the Super Bowl MVP. Seattle has a projection.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best-Selling Author

text:
A point hard to argue with both there, and in America.
Israel and Netanyahu face a political reckoning after the US midterm elections - opinion
ByDOUGLAS BLOOMFIELD
US President Donald Trump and the Republican Party weren’t the only ones to take a shellacking in the Bluenami midterm elections. Israel and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who makes no secret of his Republican leanings, were also gobsmacked by the waves.

If there was anything resembling a bipartisan consensus in this election, it was that Bibi must go, and the US-Israel alliance needs a major overhaul.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance wasted no time putting blame for the Republican losses on Israel.

The president tried to distance himself from the expected anti-Israel wave by announcing a deal with Netanyahu to halt military aid by the end of the year. “They don’t need it,” he explained. The prime minister didn’t confirm, and the White House offered no details. The Obama-era aid agreement runs through 2028.

Vance interpreted the election outcome as Republicans saying they want to “change our relationship with Israel.” He got an immediate enthusiastic endorsement from the president’s son, Donald Trump Jr. The president agreed, telling 60 Minutes, “there’s a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel.” He then took full credit for Israel’s survival: "Israel would not exist except for Donald Trump.”

A definition of tzoris is when Trump and Abdul El-Sayed, the newly elected far-left Democratic senator from Michigan, agree on halting military assistance to Israel. The senator-elect would go much further, though, including restricting or even blocking Israeli access to American technology and weapons.

El-Sayed, who will be the first Muslim in the Senate, ran on a stridently anti-Israel, anti-AIPAC (American Israel Public Affairs Committee) platform. The pro-Israel lobby group, through its PACs, spent some $30 million trying to defeat him.

Virtually his first move on winning was to call for replacing the Democratic Senate leader, Chuck Schumer, one of Israel’s most prominent supporters, with one of Israel’s most strident critics, Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.

Schumer had backed El-Sayed’s primary opponent but endorsed him for the general. Van Hollen had backed the challenger from the outset.

'An obstacle to peace'
Schumer had already moved beyond the days when he called himself “Bibi’s best friend in Washington.” More than two years ago, he said the prime minister had “lost his way” and must be replaced because he had become “an obstacle to peace.” He supports military aid restrictions.

Van Hollen, 67, has given several reasons for challenging Schumer, 75. He said the midterm elections showed voters want change, ignoring that Schumer was the architect, recruiter, and fundraiser for the Senate victories.

But Israel appears to be an underlying factor. Van Hollen has been one of the most outspoken critics of Israel’s Gaza campaign, accusing it of pursuing policies that worsen the humanitarian crisis. He wants to restrict US military assistance and levy sanctions in response to Jewish settler violence against West Bank Palestinians.

Van Hollen said he dropped his plans to run for president two years from now to unseat Schumer, but I suspect that if he loses his leadership bid, he will withdraw his withdrawal from the 2028 sweepstakes.

El-Sayed questions Israel’s right to exist as a Jewish state or “ethnostate,” as he called it. He does support the two-state solution, as do Schumer and most Americans. Netanyahu is unalterably opposed.

The Iran war and its economic impact at home were major factors in moving voters to the Democratic column. Trump and Vance sensed that coming and have hinted they feel Netanyahu pushed them into joining his long-sought war.

In the weeks before both countries’ elections (Israelis voted one week before the Americans), Netanyahu was talking about reigniting the war, a move seen to serve his political needs, not Israeli security.

Israel could also be a factor in electing the next Speaker of the House. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader and presumed shoo-in, is a long-time supporter of Israel with close ties to the Jewish community – like Schumer, he’s from Brooklyn – and may face a challenge for that reason.

A slight majority of Democrats voted this summer to cut military aid to Israel; next year the caucus will be more progressive and likely to increase the challenge. Similarly, the GOP is expected to be more isolationist.

Jeffries recognizes the wall-to-wall bipartisan support for Israel has vanished in the wake of Gaza and Iran. No longer ready to vote for unconditional aid to Israel, he has said, “The status quo is unacceptable, and we need dramatic change.”

He cited the treatment of Palestinians in the West Bank, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, Jewish settler terrorism, and Palestinian statehood.

That is consistent with the bipartisan consensus on Capitol Hill for changing the bilateral relationship. The era of wall-to-wall support is history.

AIPAC's demands for unrestricted support wound up helping elect anti-Israel candidates because it set the bar too high.

A survey by the Chicago Council on Global Affairs concluded that most Americans support decreasing or halting aid to Israel.

An Israeli friend told me the other day, “I’m not sure the Israeli government really understands the gravity of what is happening.”

An American Jewish community leader added, “There can be no reconciliation with the Democrats until Bibi goes.”

Netanyahu’s longstanding decision to abandon the Democrats to focus on evangelicals, Republicans, and the Trump followers – not unlike AIPAC – has backfired.

Republican fortunes could turn around in two years with a pink wave, but Israel’s recovery will take much longer, even if Netanyahu is replaced by a more centrist and responsible government.

Sen. Chris Coons (D-Delaware), who is expected to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee next year, said restoring bipartisan support will require “Israel making changes in policy that move in the direction of our shared values.”

Just as Israel needs new leadership, so does AIPAC, which has emerged from the midterms weakened and tarnished. Politico has reported that it will enter the 120th Congress with fewer allies.

The organization had marched in lockstep with Netanyahu for many years, only to become a pariah for many lawmakers and candidates.

If it is to regain lost respect, it must return to its bipartisan roots, get out of the money game, and stop endorsing candidates, especially bad guys (like election deniers) just because they may vote right sometimes. That will require a complete top-down rebuilding.

Under its present leadership, the once highly respected lobby has lost credibility not only among Democrats but in the Jewish community where it was seen as protecting extremists who opposed most of the priorities of Jewish voters and supported an unpopular extremist Israeli government.

Israel also must win back American Jewry, which is becoming increasingly indifferent to its welfare.

A poll for J Street, AIPAC's leftist rival, found 72% of Jewish voters backed Democratic congressional candidates in this month’s election. A similar number support sanctions on Jewish terrorists.

My generation and my parents grew up in an age of a threatened Israel fighting for survival; our children and grandchildren know it as a swaggering, muscular, nuclear-armed regional superpower. David and Goliath have switched roles.

text:
🎮 THE HISTORY OF ESPORTS IN 100 POINTS

🕹️ THE ARCADE ERA
𝟏. Spacewar!, one of the first video games, was created at MIT 🇺🇸 in 1962

𝟐. On 19 October 1972, Stanford students held the 'Intergalactic Spacewar Olympics', often called the first esports event

𝟑. The grand prize was a one-year subscription to Rolling Stone magazine

𝟒. Atari's 1980 Space Invaders Championship drew roughly 10,000 players across the US

𝟓. It was won by Rebecca Heineman, who later became a well-known game developer

𝟔. In 1981 Walter Day opened the Twin Galaxies arcade in Ottumwa, Iowa, which began tracking world record scores

𝟕. In 1982 Life magazine photographed America's top arcade players in front of Twin Galaxies

𝟖. The TV show Starcade (1982-1984) turned arcade contests into televised entertainment 📺

𝟗. The 1990 Nintendo World Championships toured 29 US cities

𝟏𝟎. Blockbuster Video ran its own World Video Game Championship in the mid-1990s

🖥️ LAN PARTIES AND THE PC BOOM
𝟏𝟏. Shooters like Doom (1993) and Quake (1996) made online and LAN multiplayer hugely popular

𝟏𝟐. DreamHack began as a small LAN party in Sweden 🇸🇪 in 1994 and later set Guinness records for the largest LAN party

𝟏𝟑. QuakeCon was first held in Texas in 1996

𝟏𝟒. At Red Annihilation in 1997, Dennis 'Thresh' Fong won John Carmack's Ferrari 328 GTS 🏎️

𝟏𝟓. The Cyberathlete Professional League (CPL) was founded in 1997

𝟏𝟔. SK Gaming, one of the oldest esports organisations, was founded in Germany 🇩🇪 in 1997

𝟏𝟕. Counter-Strike began in 1999 as a Half-Life mod made by Minh Le and Jess Cliffe

𝟏𝟖. Team Liquid started in the Netherlands 🇳🇱 in 2000 as a StarCraft fan community

𝟏𝟗. The Electronic Sports League (ESL) was founded in Cologne in 2000

𝟐𝟎. Major League Gaming (MLG) was founded in New York in 2002

𝟐𝟏. The Electronic Sports World Cup (ESWC) was first held in France 🇫🇷 in 2003

𝟐𝟐. Fnatic was founded in London 🇬🇧 in 2004

𝟐𝟑. Johnathan 'Fatal1ty' Wendel won $150,000 at the 2005 CPL World Tour finals in Painkiller

𝟐𝟒. The Championship Gaming Series (2007-2008) tried to make esports a TV league with franchised teams, but folded

🇰🇷 THE KOREAN STARCRAFT REVOLUTION
𝟐𝟓. StarCraft was released in 1998 and exploded in South Korea 🇰🇷 thanks to thousands of internet cafes called 'PC bangs'

𝟐𝟔. The Korea e-Sports Association (KeSPA) was founded in 2000

𝟐𝟕. OnGameNet, launched in 2000, was one of the first TV channels dedicated to gaming

𝟐𝟖. StarCraft finals reportedly drew crowds of tens of thousands to Busan's Gwangalli Beach

𝟐𝟗. Lim Yo-hwan, 'BoxeR', became one of esports' first true superstars

𝟑𝟎. Lee Young-ho, 'Flash', was nicknamed 'The Ultimate Weapon' for his dominance

𝟑𝟏. The World Cyber Games were launched in South Korea, with the first official edition held in Seoul in 2001

𝟑𝟐. A 2010 match-fixing scandal shook Korean StarCraft and led to lifetime bans

𝟑𝟑. StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty arrived in 2010, launching the Global StarCraft II League (GSL)

𝟑𝟒. In 2018 Canada's 🇨🇦 Sasha 'Scarlett' Hostyn became the first woman to win a major StarCraft II tournament, IEM PyeongChang

🥊 THE FIGHTING GAME COMMUNITY
𝟑𝟓. Evo grew out of Battle by the Bay, a Street Fighter tournament held in California in 1996

𝟑𝟔. It was renamed Evolution in 2002 and moved to Las Vegas in 2005

𝟑𝟕. 'Evo Moment 37' (2004): Daigo Umehara 🇯🇵 parried every hit of Justin Wong's super and won with a comeback

𝟑𝟖. That clip is often called the most famous moment in esports history

𝟑𝟗. Pakistan's 🇵🇰 Arslan Ash won both Evo Japan and Evo in Las Vegas in 2019 in Tekken 7

𝟒𝟎. Super Smash Bros. Melee, a 2001 game, still has a thriving competitive scene thanks to its grassroots community

𝟒𝟏. Capcom launched the Capcom Pro Tour for Street Fighter in 2014

🏆 THE MOBA AND STREAMING BOOM
𝟒𝟐. Defense of the Ancients (DotA) started as a Warcraft III mod in the early 2000s

𝟒𝟑. Riot Games released League of Legends in October 2009

𝟒𝟒. Fnatic won the LoL Season 1 World Championship at DreamHack in 2011, from a $100,000 prize pool

𝟒𝟓. Twitch launched in June 2011, giving esports a permanent home for live viewing 📡

𝟒𝟔. Valve's first Dota 2 International (2011) offered a then-huge $1 million first prize

𝟒𝟕. Ukraine's 🇺🇦 Natus Vincere (Na'Vi) won that first International

𝟒𝟖. Taiwan's 🇹🇼 Taipei Assassins won the LoL Season 2 Worlds in 2012 and its $1 million prize

𝟒𝟗. Counter-Strike: Global Offensive was released in August 2012

𝟓𝟎. In 2013 the US granted LoL player Danny 'Shiphtur' Le a P-1 visa, normally for pro athletes

𝟓𝟏. The 2013 Worlds final sold out the Staples Center in Los Angeles

𝟓𝟐. Lee Sang-hyeok, 'Faker', won his first world title that year with SK Telecom T1

𝟓𝟑. Faker went on to win Worlds again in 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024, a record for any player 🐐

𝟓𝟒. Fnatic won the first CS:GO Major, DreamHack Winter, in 2013

𝟓𝟓. Amazon bought Twitch in 2014 for about $970 million

𝟓𝟔. The 2014 Worlds final filled Seoul World Cup Stadium with about 40,000 fans

𝟓𝟕. In 2014 Robert Morris University in Illinois became one of the first colleges to offer esports scholarships

𝟓𝟖. The International 2014 prize pool reached about $10.9 million, mostly crowdfunded by players buying in-game items

𝟓𝟗. In 2016 China's 🇨🇳 Wings Gaming won The International and roughly $9 million

⚖️ GROWING PAINS
𝟔𝟎. In January 2015 several iBUYPOWER players were banned for fixing a CS:GO match

𝟔𝟏. That year a pro player's admission of Adderall use pushed ESL to introduce drug testing

𝟔𝟐. In 2016 a 'skin gambling' scandal hit CS:GO, leading Valve to crack down on betting sites

𝟔𝟑. Activision Blizzard bought Major League Gaming in 2015 for about $46 million

𝟔𝟒. ESPN launched a dedicated esports section in 2016

𝟔𝟓. Hearthstone, released in 2014, brought card games into the esports spotlight

𝟔𝟔. In 2018 Japan 🇯🇵 formed the Japan Esports Union to unify the country's governing bodies

💰 THE FRANCHISE AND PRIZE-POOL ERA
𝟔𝟕. The 2017 Worlds final was played at Beijing's Bird's Nest, the 2008 Olympic stadium

𝟔𝟖. Denmark's 🇩🇰 Astralis won four CS:GO Majors between 2017 and 2019

𝟔𝟗. The Overwatch League launched in 2018 with city-based teams; slots reportedly cost $20 million

𝟕𝟎. Kim Se-yeon, 'Geguri', became the Overwatch League's first female player in 2018

𝟕𝟏. League of Legends' North American league (LCS) switched to franchising in 2018

𝟕𝟐. Invictus Gaming became the first Chinese team to win LoL Worlds, in 2018

𝟕𝟑. Esports appeared as a demonstration event at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta 🇮🇩

𝟕𝟒. Epic Games pledged $100 million for Fortnite prize pools in 2018

𝟕𝟓. Europe's OG became the first team to win The International twice, in 2018 and 2019

𝟕𝟔. The International 2019 prize pool hit about $34 million

𝟕𝟕. The 2019 Fortnite World Cup in New York had a $30 million prize pool

𝟕𝟖. 16-year-old Kyle 'Bugha' Giersdorf won its solo event and $3 million 💵

𝟕𝟗. The 2019 Southeast Asian Games in the Philippines 🇵🇭 awarded medals in esports

𝟖𝟎. Riot said the 2019 Worlds final peaked at about 44 million viewers

𝟖𝟏. Call of Duty League launched in 2020 with city-based franchises

🌍 THE MODERN ERA
𝟖𝟐. The COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 forced most major events online or into empty arenas

𝟖𝟑. Riot's tactical shooter Valorant launched in June 2020

𝟖𝟒. The International 2021 prize pool reached about $40 million, the biggest in esports history

𝟖𝟓. Team Spirit won it as an underdog that had come through qualifiers

𝟖𝟔. Na'Vi, led by Oleksandr 's1mple' Kostyliev, won the 2021 PGL Major in Stockholm without dropping a map

𝟖𝟕. In 2021 China limited under-18s to three hours of online gaming a week

𝟖𝟖. Saudi Arabia's 🇸🇦 Savvy Games Group bought ESL and FACEIT in 2022 for about $1.5 billion

𝟖𝟗. Korea's DRX won LoL Worlds 2022 after starting in the play-in stage

𝟗𝟎. The Overwatch League held its final season in 2023

𝟗𝟏. Counter-Strike 2 replaced CS:GO in September 2023

𝟗𝟐. Valve stopped crowdfunding The International in 2023, and the prize pool fell to about $3 million

𝟗𝟑. The IOC held its first Olympic Esports Week in Singapore in June 2023

𝟗𝟒. Esports became a full medal event at the Asian Games in Hangzhou in 2023, with seven titles

𝟗𝟓. South Korea's LoL team won gold there, earning its players exemption from military service

𝟗𝟔. In 2024 the IOC voted to create a separate Olympic Esports Games

𝟗𝟕. Riyadh hosted the first Esports World Cup in 2024, with a prize pool above $60 million

𝟗𝟖. The 2024 Worlds final in London drew a reported peak of nearly 7 million viewers outside China

𝟗𝟗. Market researchers estimate the global esports audience at around half a billion people

𝟏𝟎𝟎. From a magazine subscription in 1972 to prize pools of tens of millions, esports grew into a global industry 🚀

text: DARTMOUTH, NS — The Nova Scotia School Board Council of Unions (NSSBCU) has  invited the provincial government to return to the bargaining table before noon on  Monday, November 23, with a new bargaining position developed in response to  members' rejection of a tentative agreement earlier this week.  “We've spent this week listening to our members, and their message is clear: they  cannot wait four years for a meaningful wage increase,” said NSSBCU Chair Nelson  Scott. “We're ready to return to the table now. With government's cooperation, we  believe we can reach an agreement our members will accept.”  Following the ratification vote, NSSBCU leaders held virtual town halls, received  hundreds of emails, spoke directly with members and collected thousands of survey  responses.  “The only wage increase government was willing to offer came on the very last day of a  four-year agreement,” said Shelley McNeil, President of CUPE Local 5047. “We've  heard from workers who love their jobs but are struggling to pay for groceries, housing  and heating. They need to be able to make ends meet now.”  CUPE Nova Scotia President Alan Linkletter announced that he is writing to Premier  Tim Houston and Minister Brendan Maguire urging government to recognize the  essential work school support workers do and negotiate a fair agreement.  NSSBCU remains committed to reaching a negotiated settlement but says job action  remains a possibility if there is no progress at the bargaining table.  “Our legal 48-hour strike notice remains in effect,” said Scott. “If we're forced to the  picket line, we'll provide 24 hours' notice to members and parents. Our priority is getting  back to the table and reaching a fair deal so we can continue supporting our school  communities.”

Subject: Building Diplomatic Relations and Strategic Partnerships with the Republic of Balochistan: An Invitation to International Recognition and Cooperation

Excellencies,
Finland declared independence from Russia in 1917 and fought for it in a civil war and then in the Winter War (1939–1940) against a vastly larger Soviet army. The nation's sisu, or perseverance, made it a symbol of determined defence.
We admire Finland's perseverance, its education system and its record of neutral diplomacy. Balochistan hopes for mutual understanding and cooperation.
Europe’s commitment to law, human rights and the self-determination of peoples is one that the Baloch people deeply respect.

The history of Balochistan
Balochistan is not a newcomer to sovereignty. The Khanate of Kalat held a distinct treaty relationship with the British Crown (1876) and was never part of British India’s princely states. On 4 August 1947, at a round-table meeting in Delhi attended by Lord Mountbatten, Mohammad Ali Jinnah and the Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan, it was agreed that Kalat (Balochistan) would become an independent sovereign state with a status different from that of the Indian princely states.
On 11 August 1947, three days before Pakistan came into being, Balochistan declared its independence from British rule. The announcement was published in the New York Times and broadcast by All India Radio on 12 August 1947. A standstill agreement with the new Dominion of Pakistan followed.

Kalat’s bicameral parliament, the Dar-ul-Awam (House of commons) and the Dar-ul-Umara (House of lords), unanimously rejected accession to Pakistan when it met in December 1947 and February 1948. On 27 March 1948 Pakistan illegally invaded and annexed Balochistan. The Baloch have never regarded this as a free act: the Khan and Jinnah were photographed together on other occasions, yet not a single photograph of the signing of the accession instrument has been published, which is consistent with our position that it was never a mutual agreement.
Since 1948 the Baloch people have continued to assert their right to independence and sovereignty, through political action, diplomatic manners and, at times, defensive armed resistance (1948, 1958, 1962, 1973–77 and since the early 2000s). Millions of Baloch, scattered across the globe but united in purpose, are raising one voice under the leadership of Hyrbyair Marri, President of the Free Balochistan Movement. They call on the nations of the world to recognize the Republic of Balochistan as an independent state, a recognition it has earned and rightfully deserves.

The Baloch nation has long suffered the plunder of its resources, enforced disappearances, ethnic cleansing, and relentless repression by Pakistan. Across the western part of Balochistan, the Baloch people face the same fate under Iranian rule: fabricated encounters, mass executions, expulsion from their own land, and the denial of birth certificates and legal identity, a deliberate effort to erase their existence.

The significance of Balochistan
Balochistan sits where South Asia, Central Asia and the Middle East meet, on the Arabian Sea coast just outside the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil passes. It is a natural gateway for global trade. Two globally important deep-sea ports lie on the Baloch coast: Chabahar, which is under Iran’s illegal rule, and Gwadar, which is under Pakistan’s unlawful rule. Beneath the land lie Balochistan’s mineral resources include copper, gold, chromite, coal, natural gas, lead, zinc, barite, iron ore, limestone, gypsum, marble, granite, onyx, magnesite, sulphur, fluorite, antimony, manganese, bauxite, celestite, rock salt, silica sand, fuller’s earth, lapis lazuli, agate, and reported traces of uranium and rare earth elements of strategic value, including the Reko Diq and Saindak deposits and the Sui gas field.
Because the Republic of Balochistan declared independence on 11 August 1947, we, the Baloch, consider ourselves independent. A free, Secular, democratic and stable Balochistan is vital for regional and global peace and for connectivity between the Indian Ocean and the heartland of Eurasia.

Balochistan offers: Building Partnerships for Peace, Security, and Sustainable Development

Finland is a new NATO member with a long border with Russia and a strong tradition of preparedness. It is strengthening its defense and its industry with characteristic determination. The country is also a leader in clean technology and innovation. Its approach shows that security and sustainability can go hand in hand. A free, stable Balochistan, at the meeting-point of Eurasia and the Indian Ocean, can be a natural partner in this journey. It can contribute to peace, security and connectivity across the region.

The Republic of Balochistan offers your country:
• Education and clean technology: Finnish education, cleantech and telecommunications expertise.
• Defense and security: training, procurement and industrial cooperation, within the limits of international law.
• Technology and innovation: joint research, digital infrastructure and training partnerships between your institutions and Baloch universities.
• Energy: long-term, preferential supply agreements for natural gas and other energy resources from Balochistan, and joint development of its large solar and wind potential.

Our request
On behalf of the Republic of Balochistan, we respectfully ask your Government to:
1. Recognize the Republic of Balochistan as an independent state and establish diplomatic relations;
2. Support appropriate observer-level engagement for Balochistan at the United Nations and, in line with each Organization’s own procedures, at the European Union, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and the African Union. As a member of the European Union, your Government’s voice would carry real weight.
3. Stand with the Baloch in nation-building: education, health, infrastructure, technology, defense and security.

The commitments in this letter are those of the Republic of Balochistan as it takes up the effective exercise of sovereignty over its territory and resources; we make them in good faith so that your Government can plan with us from the outset.
Partnership with Balochistan is of real benefit to your country and to the world. We would welcome the opportunity to meet your representatives at the earliest convenience.

With our highest consideration,
THE REPUBLIC OF BALOCHISTAN

In Texas, you can see them. Under a 2023 law (HB 5180, Elec. Code 1.012), anyone may inspect the original voted ballots starting day 61: Jan 3, 2027, a Sunday, so in practice Monday, Jan 4. Until then they stay locked up. Cast vote records and ballot images (where kept) open the day after the final canvass. For statewide races, that's the state canvass, due Nov 21-Dec 7. Counties must redact anything that ties a voter to a ballot. Ask your county elections office.

⭕️ Trump Outlines China Summit Results, Iran Strategy, UN Reform and Major Economic Priorities

President Donald Trump held an extensive White House news conference Friday following his return from China, addressing international diplomacy, nuclear security, Iran, trade, artificial intelligence and the U.S. economy.

Key Takeaways:

• Historic Trilateral Summit: Trump praised his meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, defending direct diplomacy between the world’s leading nuclear powers as essential to preventing conflict.

• United Nations Reform: The United States, Russia and China agreed to pursue changes to the UN aimed at improving its effectiveness in addressing international security threats. Specific reforms have not yet been announced.

• Nuclear Security: The three leaders committed to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. No binding arms-control agreement was reached.

• Iran: Trump said Tehran wants an agreement but has not offered terms acceptable to Washington. He reiterated his preference for a lasting deal as tensions over Iran’s military capabilities continue.

• Ukraine: The summit included discussions about ending the war, although no ceasefire or peace agreement was announced.

• Global Energy: Washington, Moscow and Beijing pledged to increase supplies of refined petroleum products and support more stable international energy markets.

• China Trade: Trump highlighted improved relations with Beijing and new economic cooperation, including discussions involving trade, technology and American exports.

• U.S. Agriculture: Trump promoted an agreement under which the Philippines would increase purchases of American agricultural and energy products, benefiting U.S. farmers.

• Artificial Intelligence and Data Centers: Trump announced plans to impose substantial financial penalties on American companies building data centers overseas, arguing that advanced computing infrastructure should remain in the United States. Implementation details remain unclear.

• Energy Prices: Trump highlighted falling gasoline prices, saying the national average has declined approximately 60 cents per gallon over the past month.

• Midterm Elections: Trump acknowledged Republican losses, arguing that the administration failed to communicate its economic accomplishments effectively and that the results would have differed had he been on the ballot.

📌Bottom Line: The administration is presenting the China summit as a major diplomatic achievement, with commitments on nuclear risk reduction, UN reform and energy cooperation. The most consequential questions remain whether those commitments produce enforceable agreements and how Washington proceeds on Iran and Ukraine.

text:
Was 13-Year-Old Mary Phagan Raped by Leo Frank? What the Medical Evidence, Jim Conley's Testimony, and the Prosecution's Closing Arguments Reveal

A Response to Sacamano Says (@SacamanoSays)

Sacamano Says (@SacamanoSays) recently wrote:

"Mary Phagan wasn't raped, still a virgin from the autopsy. I don't think dying would've stopped Conley since he wasn't White."

The claim that Mary Phagan was never raped, supposedly proved by her autopsy, has been repeated in hagiographical accounts written to rehabilitate Leo Frank. The problem with this argument is that it overlooks much of the evidence presented during Frank's July and August 1913 murder trial.

I encourage @SacamanoSays and everyone interested in the case to read the original Brief of Evidence, particularly the sworn testimony of Dr. John Wesley Hurt, Dr. Henry Frederick Harris, Jim Conley, and the witnesses who examined Mary Phagan's body and clothing. Then read the closing arguments of Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey and Frank's defense attorneys.

The prosecution argued that Leo Frank sexually assaulted Mary Phagan after she refused his advances and then strangled her to prevent her from revealing what had happened. Dorsey explicitly accused Frank of raping her.

I believe the surviving evidence gives substantial grounds for considering that accusation. It does not, however, establish every detail of the alleged assault beyond dispute. We should examine what the witnesses actually said rather than replace their testimony with an assertion that the autopsy ruled out rape.

Saturday, April 26, 1913: Mary Phagan's Final Trip to the Pencil Factory

Mary Phagan was 13 years old when she was murdered on Saturday, April 26, 1913, Confederate Memorial Day in Atlanta, Georgia.

She worked in the metal department of the National Pencil Company at 37–41 South Forsyth Street. That morning, she traveled into downtown Atlanta to collect approximately $1.20 in wages owed to her.

Her last known encounter with Leo Frank, the factory superintendent, occurred shortly after noon when she entered his second-floor office to receive her pay.

Frank acknowledged paying her. He maintained that she left his office alive and that he never saw her again.

The prosecution presented a different account. It argued that Frank followed Mary toward the rear metal department, made unwanted sexual advances, struck her when she resisted, sexually assaulted her, and finally strangled her.

The question of sexual assault was central to the prosecution's explanation of why Mary Phagan was killed.

Friday, April 25: Why Did Mary Have to Collect Her Own Pay?

The day before the murder, factory employee Helen Ferguson testified that she asked Frank for Mary Phagan's pay envelope.

According to Ferguson, Frank refused to release it.

Ferguson had previously collected Mary's wages, so the prosecution argued that Frank's refusal could have been part of an effort to ensure Mary returned to the factory personally the next day.

Dorsey later incorporated this incident into his argument that Frank had planned an opportunity to be alone with her.

The defense disputed Ferguson's account and offered testimony about the factory's payroll procedures. Her testimony therefore supports the prosecution's theory only if her account is accepted. It does not independently establish that Frank planned an assault (BOE, 1).

Sunday, April 27: Mary Phagan's Body Is Discovered

At approximately 3:00 a.m. on Sunday, April 27, 1913, factory nightwatchman Newt Lee discovered Mary Phagan's body in the basement of the National Pencil Company building.

Her body lay near a pile of refuse. A cord was tightly drawn around her neck. Another piece of cloth had been used around her head and neck.

Her face and head showed injuries, and her clothing was damaged.

The location of the body did not necessarily establish where the original attack occurred. The prosecution maintained that Mary had been attacked on the second floor and that her body was later transported into the basement.

What did the medical examiners find?

The Torn Underclothing and Bloodstains

W. H. Gheesling, the undertaker who removed Mary's body from the factory basement at approximately 3:50 a.m. on April 27, testified about the condition of her clothing.

He observed dried blood on her underclothing and described the right leg of her drawers as having been split or torn along the seam.

Drawers were the undergarments worn beneath women's and girls' dresses in 1913.

Gheesling also found blood in Mary's hair and described the serious wound on the back of her head.

During the trial, other witnesses described damaged clothing, including a broken stocking supporter. A stocking supporter was a strap or fastening used to hold stockings in place.

The Atlanta Journal of Wednesday, July 30, 1913, reported that the police observed damaged undergarments and a broken stocking supporter (BOE, 1). (AJ, 2).

None of these observations, considered separately, proves rape. Clothing can be damaged during an attack, while a body is dragged, or through other circumstances.

But the torn garments, bloodstains, and injuries were physical evidence that the prosecution was entitled to place before the jury.

Dorsey later used those very garments to argue that Mary had resisted a sexual assault.

Dr. John Wesley Hurt Examines Mary's Body

Dr. John Wesley Hurt, the Fulton County physician, examined Mary Phagan on Sunday morning, April 27, 1913.

Hurt testified that he found a serious scalp wound, a bruised eye, scratches, and evidence of strangulation.

He also found blood on her drawers and around her genital area.

Hurt observed that her hymen was not intact. The hymen is a fold of tissue near the opening of the vagina. Its condition cannot reliably establish whether a person has previously engaged in sexual intercourse.

Hurt further testified that the vagina appeared somewhat enlarged and that penetration shortly before death was one possible explanation.

He did not identify when the hymen had been altered or establish what caused the blood.

Under cross-examination, Hurt acknowledged that the appearance of the blood was consistent with menstruation. He found no outward signs of rape and declined to express an opinion on whether Mary had been raped or had previously engaged in intercourse.

This was a limitation of Hurt's findings, not a declaration that rape was impossible (BOE, 1).

May 5, 1913: Dr. Henry Frederick Harris Performs a Second Examination

Nine days after Mary Phagan was murdered, Dr. Henry Frederick Harris examined her body on Monday, May 5, 1913.

Harris was secretary of the Georgia State Board of Health.

His investigation included a more extensive internal examination than Hurt's original inspection, including microscopic study of genital tissue.

A microscope allowed him to inspect changes in tissue that were not visible during an ordinary external examination.

This is where the medical evidence becomes especially relevant to the question of sexual violence.

What Dr. Harris Found Inside Mary's Vagina

Dr. Harris testified under oath for the State in the Fulton County Superior Court in Atlanta on Friday afternoon, August 1, 1913. His testimony continued during the following week.

In the official Brief of Evidence, page 48, Harris stated that he found no spermatozoa. He also reported finding evidence of violence inside the vagina.

He described the epithelium as having been pulled loose and completely detached in some places. He further described dilated blood vessels and hemorrhaging in the surrounding tissues.

These words require some explanation.

Epithelium is the layer of cells covering surfaces inside and outside the body. In this case, Harris was referring to the lining of Mary's vagina.

Hemorrhage means bleeding. The bleeding Harris described was within the tissues, not simply blood lying on the surface of the body.

Dilated blood vessels are blood vessels that have widened.

Harris interpreted these findings as evidence of injuries inflicted while Mary's blood was still circulating.

On page 49, he estimated that the genital injuries had occurred approximately 10 to 15 minutes before death.

He also identified evidence of violence near the hymen.

Most significantly, Harris attributed the tissue injuries to violence occurring shortly before Mary's death, rather than ordinary changes caused by menstruation (BOE, 1).

Why the Timing of the Injuries Deserves Attention

Harris did not simply find blood and assume Mary had been raped.

He examined tissue beneath the vaginal surface and considered the condition of the blood vessels, inflammation, and hemorrhaging.

He believed the observed changes indicated an injury sustained while Mary was alive.

In his opinion, the genital injuries occurred shortly before the strangulation that caused her death.

That finding fit the prosecution's theory that the sexual attack and murder occurred during the same episode.

However, Harris's estimate was a medical opinion, not a stopwatch measurement. The examination occurred nine days after the murder, and Mary's body had already been embalmed.

His conclusions about precisely when the injuries occurred could be questioned.

Even so, the record does not justify pretending that Harris found no injuries or that his testimony ruled out sexual violence (BOE, 1).

Did Menstruation Explain the Genital Injuries?

The defense had an alternative explanation for some of the blood observed on Mary's body and clothing.

Dr. Hurt acknowledged that the external blood could have been menstrual.

But Harris drew attention to the condition of the vaginal walls themselves.

In his testimony, Harris maintained that ordinary menstruation could not account for the particular blood-vessel changes and discoloration he observed.

This was the medical disagreement the jury had to consider.

Blood on underclothing could have several explanations. Bleeding inside damaged vaginal tissue raised a different medical question.

Harris believed the tissue findings resulted from violence. Hurt was less willing to draw that conclusion.

The existence of these competing opinions is a reason to examine the evidence carefully, not to declare that the autopsy proved no sexual assault occurred (BOE, 1).

No Spermatozoa Does Not Mean No Rape

Sacamano Says places considerable weight on the assertion that Mary was still a virgin.

But there are two separate questions here.

The first is whether the examination recovered spermatozoa.

The second is whether Mary was sexually assaulted.

Spermatozoa are male reproductive cells, commonly called sperm. They may be present in semen, but a sexual assault does not always involve ejaculation.

A rapist may fail to ejaculate, may ejaculate somewhere else, or may use a finger or other object to penetrate the victim.

Modern forensic guidance recognizes that the failure to recover semen does not establish that a sexual assault never occurred (NSVRC, 3).

In Mary's case, Harris performed his examination nine days after the murder and after the body had undergone embalming.

He found no spermatozoa.

That result cannot establish that no sexual violence occurred.

Nor does it settle whether penile penetration occurred. Harris acknowledged that the injuries might have been caused by a finger or another means (BOE, 1).

The stronger argument is that his findings were consistent with genital violence, not that they identified the exact method of an assault.

Could an Autopsy Prove Mary Phagan Was a Virgin?

No.

The medical language used in 1913 sometimes referred to a normal or virginal uterus.

That terminology does not establish a person's sexual history.

Likewise, the hymen is not a reliable record of whether intercourse has occurred.

The World Health Organization, UN Women, and the United Nations Human Rights Office explained in their October 2018 statement that no physical examination can reliably prove a history of vaginal intercourse (WHO, 4).

Even accepting the claim that Mary had never engaged in sexual intercourse before April 26, 1913, how would that prove she was not assaulted on the day of her murder?

It would not.

The assertion that she was a virgin before the crime is not evidence disproving an assault during the crime.

August 1, August 6, and August 7: Harris Testifies in Court

Harris first appeared for the State on Friday afternoon, August 1, 1913.

He became ill during his testimony and was excused before the defense completed its questioning.

The Atlanta Constitution of Saturday, August 2, reported that Harris could not conclusively say whether Mary had been sexually violated, although he found indications suggesting violence (AC, 5).

The Atlanta Journal gave a more cautious account in its August 3 summary, saying that Harris had found evidence of violence but had not established a completed criminal assault (AJ, 6).

Harris returned to the witness stand on Wednesday afternoon, August 6. He continued describing the medical findings and was excused at approximately 5:00 p.m. because of his weakened condition.

He resumed his cross-examination on Thursday, August 7.

The Atlanta Journal of August 7 reported that Harris reaffirmed his opinion concerning violence inflicted before Mary's death, while the defense challenged his medical conclusions (AJ, 7).

I would not disregard the cautious newspaper accounts. They show the limits of Harris's findings. But those limits do not support the absolute assertion that no sexual assault occurred.

Monday, August 4: Jim Conley Describes Mary Phagan's Resistance

The medical evidence was only one part of the prosecution's case.

On Monday morning, August 4, 1913, Jim Conley, the National Pencil Company sweeper, took the witness stand for the prosecution.

Conley testified that Frank had arranged for him to watch the first-floor entrance and close the door when signaled.

According to Conley, he saw Mary Phagan enter the factory and later heard a woman scream from the direction of the second-floor metal department.

Conley said he subsequently heard Frank signal him and went upstairs.

There, according to his testimony, Frank appeared agitated and held a cord in his hands.

Conley testified that Frank told him he had accompanied Mary toward the metal department and had wanted sexual contact with her.

The critical statement, attributed by Conley to Frank, was:

"I wanted to be with the little girl, and she refused me"

Conley said Frank then admitted striking Mary so hard that she fell and injured her head.

This was not Conley claiming that he personally witnessed a rape. It was Conley reporting what he said Frank had told him after the attack.

That limits the testimony, but it also explains why it was so incriminating if believed.

Frank was allegedly admitting that he approached Mary sexually, that she refused, and that he struck her (BOE, 1). (AJ, 8).

What Did Conley Say He Heard Before Frank Summoned Him?

Conley testified that he heard footsteps moving away from Frank's office toward the metal department.

He then heard a woman's scream.

He did not claim to have watched the actual assault. He placed himself downstairs during the episode.

Conley described later finding Mary lying in the metal department with a cord around her neck and assisting Frank in moving her body.

According to the prosecution, this account linked the sexual advance, the violent struggle, the injuries, and the removal of the body.

It also supplied the alleged motive for the murder.

Conley was an interested witness who admitted having withheld information and lied during the investigation. His credibility was heavily contested.

During cross-examination on Tuesday, August 5, defense attorney Luther Rosser challenged the additions to Conley's account, including his earlier statement that Frank had picked up the girl and let her fall.

The Atlanta Journal reported these challenges and the differences between Conley's affidavits and courtroom testimony (AJ, 9).

Anyone arguing from Conley's testimony should acknowledge those issues. But anyone dismissing the sexual-assault allegation must also address what Conley actually told the jury.

The Prosecution's Theory: Mary Refused Frank and Was Attacked

The prosecution's explanation of the crime was that Leo Frank had sexual intentions toward Mary Phagan.

The State argued that when Mary refused him, Frank became violent.

The prosecution further maintained that Frank sexually assaulted Mary and then strangled her because he feared the consequences if she survived and reported what had happened.

This was presented as a motive for murder, not a separate medical finding.

The doctors testified about wounds and physical conditions. Conley supplied the alleged account of Frank's conduct and admission. Dorsey combined the evidence into the State's explanation of the murder.

That explanation must be evaluated against the entire record, but it cannot fairly be described as a case in which sexual assault was never alleged or supported by evidence.

Friday, August 22: Dorsey Opens His Closing Argument

Hugh M. Dorsey began his final argument for the prosecution on Friday, August 22, 1913.

His address continued on Saturday, August 23, and concluded on Monday, August 25.

Dorsey argued that the murder arose from Frank's sexual intentions toward Mary Phagan.

He also referred to testimony concerning Frank's alleged conduct toward female employees and argued that the jury should consider that evidence when evaluating his motive.

The Atlanta Constitution of August 23 reported Dorsey's attack on Frank's character, including his reference to testimony concerning lasciviousness (AC, 10).

Lasciviousness is an older word describing sexual behavior or desires regarded as improper.

Those character allegations were not independent proof that Frank raped Mary. They were part of Dorsey's attempt to persuade the jury that the sexual motive he alleged was consistent with Frank's conduct.

Saturday, August 23: Dorsey Uses Mary's Torn Clothing as Evidence

On Saturday, August 23, 1913, Dorsey continued his argument before the jury in the Fulton County Superior Court.

He pointed to Mary's damaged clothing and the medical testimony.

According to the Atlanta Journal, Dorsey demanded that the jurors examine the torn garments and stockings and consider why they were in that condition.

He connected those physical exhibits with his argument that Mary had resisted Frank.

The Journal reported that Mary Phagan's mother, Mrs. J. W. Coleman, became overwhelmed with emotion while Dorsey discussed her daughter's death.

Dorsey was not simply asking the jury to believe that Frank had wanted to approach Mary sexually.

He was arguing that a sexual assault had taken place and that Mary's resistance led to her murder (AJ, 11).

Dorsey's Accusation: Frank Ravished Mary Phagan

The word ravished appears repeatedly in the contemporary accounts of Dorsey's closing address.

In this context, ravished meant raped or sexually violated by force.

Dorsey used that word when describing what he believed Frank had done.

In the published text of his closing argument, Dorsey accused Frank of striking Mary after she refused him and then sexually assaulting her while she was helpless.

He told the jury:

"you struck her and you ravished her"

This was the prosecutor's accusation, not a statement by a medical witness.

Dorsey also argued that Frank gagged and strangled Mary to prevent her from telling anyone about the attack (Dorsey, 12).

The accusation was explicit. It was not an inference invented by writers many decades later.

The Atlanta Georgian Reports Dorsey's Accusation

The Atlanta Georgian of Sunday, August 24, 1913, published an extensive report of Dorsey's closing argument.

It described how the prosecutor held Mary's bloodstained garments before the jury and asked the jurors to examine the physical evidence.

The newspaper reported that Dorsey called Mary a ravished girl and argued that she had resisted Frank's sexual demands.

He pointed to the torn underclothing, blood, and the circumstances of the killing.

Dorsey argued that Frank had first attempted to obtain sexual contact, then attacked Mary when she resisted, and subsequently strangled her.

This was a complete prosecution theory of a sexually motivated murder (AG, 13).

The Bloodstained Garments Were Shown to the Jury

One point deserves particular attention.

Mary's damaged underclothing was not simply a detail mentioned in later books.

It was physical evidence discussed at the trial and displayed during Dorsey's closing address.

The State asked jurors to consider the torn garment, bloodstains, and broken stocking supporter together with Harris's findings of genital tissue injuries.

The evidence did not establish the precise source of every bloodstain.

Nevertheless, the State argued that the condition of Mary's clothing was consistent with a struggle during a sexual assault.

That argument had a factual foundation in the testimony of the men who examined her body.

It was for the jury to determine how much weight to give that evidence (BOE, 1). (AJ, 11). (AG, 13).

Even Frank's Defense Lawyers Argued That Mary Had Been Ravished

There is another fact that should be considered before repeating the assertion that Mary Phagan was never raped.

During their closing arguments, Frank's own attorneys advanced a theory that Jim Conley had attacked Mary, robbed her, and sexually assaulted her.

The Atlanta Journal of Friday, August 22, 1913, reported Luther Rosser arguing that Conley had taken Mary's money, pushed her into the elevator shaft, and ravished her afterward.

Rosser used this theory to argue that Conley, rather than Frank, had committed the crime.

In other words, the defense did not limit itself to arguing that Mary had never been sexually assaulted.

It offered an alternative account in which Conley was the sexual assailant.

That does not prove Rosser's accusation was true. Attorneys sometimes argue alternative theories, and their closing statements are not evidence.

But it shows that sexual assault was part of the competing explanations presented to the jury in August 1913.

The State blamed Frank. The defense blamed Conley.

Neither theory can be dismissed by claiming that the autopsy proved Mary could not have been raped (AJ, 14).

Monday, August 25: The Prosecution Makes Its Final Appeal

On Monday, August 25, 1913, Dorsey completed his closing address.

The Atlanta Journal reported that he returned to his argument that Mary had refused Frank's sexual demands and died resisting him.

Dorsey urged the jury to convict Frank of murder.

The jury began deliberating that afternoon and returned a guilty verdict after approximately four hours.

The jury convicted Frank of Mary's murder, not under a separate rape indictment.

This matters when describing what the legal proceedings established.

The conviction establishes what the jury decided about the murder charge. It does not constitute a separate verdict that every allegation of sexual assault was independently proven (AJ, 15).

$CRWV 

Notes from CoreWeave CDO Brannan McBee’s appearance at TomorrowX:

The stock price is in a very different place than it was, what has changed in last 14 days?

Lot of macro change obviously, but fundamentally the business has not changed, the business has executed, all within a demand environment that continues to accelerate. No other way to describe it.

Quick recap of Q3:

Have been able to stand up over 1.7 GW of revenue generating GPUs, did 3.7 billion in revenue in Q3, more than 20 billion in ARR.

Enabled by product and team, showing up every day and getting infrastructure in the hands of consumers and doing so at scale.

Why is CoreWeave technically different and more capable?

Uses analogy: like walking in a Toyota factory and saying why can’t you make a Model Y, they say well of course we can, here is a Prius with a battery, both are EVs but one is purpose built as an EV.

It’s who their suppliers are, data center providers, GPU providers, etc, the overwhelming support is because of their product differentiation.

Says he brings lens of risk management to the business, one way they have done that is focused on success based capex, not speculatively buying GPUs. Waits for committed take or pay contracts.

You have all this compute coming off contract, to the tune of 100,000 GPUs in 2027, massive set of infrastructure that is fully amortized, what is so interesting is all of the use cases.

The client, in a very diversified way, is saying they want H100s and a specific skew of compute because they are optimized for a specific workload and task.

Useful life of compute depreciates at an average of six years, but it can extend beyond that.

Thinks best risk adjusted approach is to derisk capex through long term contracts. 

Backlog fully funds their entire debt stack across the business today. Not the first company to do this, first to do it in tech sector for GPUs, first to use GPUs as collateral in a debt facility. That was the enablement of project financing for the space.

Has CoreWeave thought at all about compute futures?

Yes, we are synthetically doing it today because we have these long term take or pay agreements. Knows it has been priced, less risk over time, been accessing the credit market.

Not fungible yet today though, says H100 in one place operates different from H100 in other case, needs to look like oil in his opinion to be a commodity market.

What should we be watching in terms of signals?

Most important signal is execution, at the end of the day you have to show up and execute. Show up, bring it online, deliver on time. Having 1.7 GW makes them one of the largest operators of this compute on the planet, executing with few peers that are out there.

130,000 GPUS coming off next year, some are Blackwells, not a crazy thought that they could get a prepayment for Blackwells coming offline next year.

Gavin says that they could probably get a pretty big prepayment in February of next year for Blackwells.
