text:
Austin & America lost a legend yesterday.

Admiral Bobby Inman was one of the giants of American public service, a driving force behind Austin's transformation into a high-tech powerhouse, and one of the most generous and remarkable people I've ever had the privilege of knowing.

But to me, he'll always be the man who believed in two young entrepreneurs when we barely knew what we were doing.

Many years ago, when my best friend Ingrid Vanderveldt, M. Arch, MBA and I were launching our first startup, the Admiral took us under his wing.

I'll never forget sitting across from him, soaking up decades of wisdom, his calming presence, and that infectious smile. No matter how uncertain things felt, we always walked away from those meetings with more confidence, a clearer perspective, & the belief that we could actually pull this off.

Ingrid once asked him how we could ever repay him for everything he'd done for us. His response:

"All I want in return is that you share what you gain and learn with as many others as you can."

A man who had served at the highest levels of American intelligence, leading the NSA & serving as deputy director of the CIA, who helped lay the foundation for Austin's technology industry, & who still found the time to mentor two young entrepreneurs trying to find their way.

His generosity was extraordinary. His wisdom was priceless. His work ethic was second to none.

But I also got to know another side of the Admiral.

Sitting alongside him at University of Texas football games, watching his beloved Longhorns through thick & thin. Hearing about his passion for skiing and the joy he found in spending time with his family. 

Those are the memories I'll treasure just as much as the business lessons.

I'm especially grateful to have known the Admiral through the years and to count his son, Tom Inman, among my very best friends. Anytime I asked the Admiral about Tom, his face would light up with an ear-to-ear smile. You could see the pride and love he had for his son.

So much of the Admiral lives on thru Tom. That same generosity, infectious smile, genuine kindness, and unwavering commitment to helping others. Tom is an extraordinary man in his own right, and seeing the beautiful family he and Marianne Inman are raising with their two children is a testament to the values his father lived by.

Admiral Bobby Inman's legacy will be felt for generations. Not just through the institutions he led, the industries he helped build, or the city he helped transform, but through the countless people whose lives he touched along the way.

For us Austinites who love our city dearly, perhaps the greatest tribute we can pay him is to honor that simple request he made of Ingrid and me all those years ago.

Share what you learn. Help others succeed. Carry it forward.

Thank you, Admiral. For believing in us, for leading by example, and for showing us what a lifetime of service, generosity, and leadership really looks like.

Hook 'em, Admiral. 🤘

text:
Behind the public debates, lawsuits, and safety pledges, Big Tech has quietly built the most complex financial web in modern history.

Over the past three years, AI has evolved from a race for better models into a massive network of circular contracts, compute commitments, and multi-billion-dollar guarantees.

Here is how we got here—and what happens when heavy regulation and market reality collide with this house of cards:

1. The Timeline: From Ideological Debates to $100B+ Guarantee.

- 2023–2024: The Split & "Invest-to-Spend" Begins

Open-source vs. closed-source debates dominate the headlines while Elon Musk sues OpenAI over its non-profit mission (a suit eventually tossed in 2026 on statute-of-limitations grounds). Behind the scenes, Microsoft, Google, and Amazon Pioneer a simple loop: invest billions in AI labs, and have those labs spend it right back on cloud compute.

- 2025: Mega-Contracts & Equity Warrants
The numbers go parabolic. OpenAI commits to $250B in Azure spend; Anthropic locks in massive multi-cloud deals with AWS, Google, and Microsoft. Meanwhile, chipmakers like AMD issue penny-warrants tied directly to gigawatt-scale GPU purchases—meaning the more chips AI labs buy, the more of the chipmaker they own.

- 2026: Off-Balance-Sheet Guarantees & National Security Clashes
Equity isn't enough anymore. Chip and cloud giants step in as literal financial guarantors. Nvidia signs a staggering $105B payment guarantee backing OpenAI’s 20-year data center lease in Ohio (on the condition it uses Nvidia hardware) and backstops billions in unsold capacity for neoclouds.

At the same time, ideological debates turn existential: Anthropic clashes with the Pentagon over military AI guardrails, sparking a brief federal ban and an unprecedented wave of support from rival engineers at OpenAI and Google.

2. The Systemic Risks Under Tighter Regulation

With the EU AI Act in full force, US state-level AI laws rolling out, and antitrust regulators circling, this circular model faces four major breaking points:

- Circular Revenue Contagion: Tech giants book revenue from startups funded by their own investments and backstopped by their own balance sheets. Analysts estimate the current infrastructure buildout requires ~$6T in annual end-user AI revenue by 2031, while real-world adoption sits closer to $1.2T–$1.8T. If a major lab defaults, guarantors like Nvidia and hyperscalers eat tens of billions in contingent liabilities—a modern echo of the 2000 telecom vendor-financing crash.

- Antitrust & "De Facto Cartel" Lawsuits: Exclusive compute locks and "safety pacing" agreements have drawn major antitrust class-actions in 2026, accusing top labs of colluding to slow down competition and starve smaller players of chips.

- Crushing Compliance & Copyright Costs: Following Anthropic’s $1.5B author copyright settlement and ongoing publisher lawsuits, scraping the open web for free is over. Mandatory audits and licensing fees are squeezing margins hard.

- Geopolitical Whiplash: Relying on massive defense and government contracts to absorb excess compute leaves AI labs vulnerable to sudden political shifts and federal blacklists.

The Bottom Line:

AI isn't just a software revolution anymore—it’s a leveraged infrastructure bet. Whether it turns into the next industrial boom or a 2000-style telecom bust depends on whether real-world value catches up before the guarantees come due.

$GOOGL: Alphabet is spending faster than it earns, and the model hasn't caught up with that yet. Here is the VecViz read, a news review, and what each 21-day tail would take.

Model date 11/19/26, close $272.66. Initial VNA Target Price $303.17 (+11.19%), but agentic review takes it to $282.10. V-Score +6 on a -12..+12 scale. Held in 47.22% of VecViz model portfolios. 21-day bands: 99D $200.77, EDB $259.71, EUB $278.02, 99U $346.72.

THE REVIEW
– NEW: AI capex outruns cash flow, funded by debt and stock sales. Bearish/Intensifying. Q3 free cash flow was -$9.1B, the second negative quarter in a row, on $51.4B of capex. Alphabet raised $28.7B in notes and sold $12.4B of stock through its ATM, has bought back no stock in 2026, and says 2027 capex will "increase significantly." The catalogue didn't have it.
– Kept at Bullish/Intensifying, already the strongest setting: TPU sales, frontier-model leadership and cloud demand. Gemini 4 Carbon tops most benchmarks, Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7B, and Anthropic's IPO filing shows $121.3B of compute committed to Google.
– Kept at Bearish/Steady: AI Mode monetisation (ads now scale inside AI Mode, but ChatGPT reports about a fifth of Google's search volume) and the search antitrust ruling (the ad-tech breakup was rejected 9/2; the search appeal is pending).
Result: target $303.17 -> $282.10.
The judgement call is the trend on the new event. Call it Steady instead and the target is $291.10. I chose Intensifying because cash burn deepened from Q2 to Q3 and 2027 spending is guided higher.

THE DOWNSIDE TAIL
The 99D is $200.77 (-26.37%). That is 1.12x Sigma's equivalent and the 37.36th percentile of GOOGL's own 273-date history, so this tail is deeper than usual for the stock.
Geometry: 12 of 14 Vector Sets (92.33% of strength weighting) contain it, all but VS4 and VS14. The closest-centred channel, VS11, is drawn off the 11/24/08 and 3/28/18 bottoms and the 2/4/25 top at $206.38. Its standalone target is $269.28.

Do that on top of my review and it reaches $172.37, past the tail. A milder version, where the AI lead stops being rewarded (TPU and model leadership go Neutral), gives $235.61, short of it. The AI tape is already weak: the Nasdaq hit a seven-month low after Anthropic's debut.

THE UPSIDE TAIL
The 99U is $346.72 (+27.16%). That is 1.16x Sigma and the 88.28th percentile of its own history, so the upside is fatter than usual.
Only VS1, VS2 and VS4 (30.27% of weighting) contain it. Every other set tops out below it, and that is the asymmetry. VS1 is the closest-centred channel, anchored on the 3/28/18 and 4/8/25 bottoms and the 5/13/26 top at $402.62. Its standalone target is $501.96.

– Monetisation: AI Mode ads close the gap with classic search, and that event turns Bullish/Intensifying: $314.52.
– Plus relief on spending, with the capex event going Neutral: $335.59.
Neither reaches the tail. The fewest-changes path flips a 2020-21 pandemic event, which is arithmetic, not a story. Three brand-new Bullish/Intensifying events would get the catalogue baseline to $366.39.
Calendar: FOMC 12/8-9, with a December hike close to fully priced. Q4 results and the 2027 capex number come in early February, after the window closes around 12/21, so relief on spending can only arrive early through a pre-announcement.

BULLISH DIVERSIFIERS
All have V-Score > 0, VNA upside > 0 and EUB > 0, at EqLiq 5+.
– $COP V-Score +6, VNA upside 12.41%. Oil, not ads; caveat: a deep 95D.
– $CVX +3, 7.92%. Oil major.
– $APA +2, 30.81%. Oil E&P.
I did not review these names' own VecEvent catalogues.

THE TAKEAWAY
The model still likes GOOGL, but adding the cash-burn story trims the target from $303.17 to $282.10. Most channels sit around the 99D and only three reach the 99U, and no news route I could build gets to the upside tail in 21 days.

The US Army Offered Soldiers Four Days to Play GTA VI. The Price? Up to Six Years of Their Lives.

Somewhere in Georgia, an American military officer realized that the prospect of stealing imaginary cars, shooting imaginary people and committing imaginary crimes might persuade soldiers to spend a few more years preparing for the real thing.

And it worked.

At Fort Stewart, the US Army's 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion offered soldiers a special four-day pass to celebrate the release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

One small condition.

They had to reenlist for another TWO TO SIX YEARS.

Four days of freedom in exchange for up to six years of military service.

Forty-three soldiers accepted the offer, according to the US Army.

Some also received substantial financial bonuses, including one soldier who reportedly collected more than $60,000.

The American military has spent decades investing unimaginable sums of money in technology designed to make killing people more efficient.

Now it's using a video game about stealing cars and killing people to persuade its employees to stay.

In GTA, you can steal a car, crash into a police barricade, slaughter a small army, die spectacularly and return five minutes later to do it all again.

Your mother doesn't receive a folded American flag.

Your children don't spend their childhood waiting for someone who will never come home.

Nobody has to identify your remains.

The consequences disappear when you switch off the console.

Real war has no reset button.

But the recruitment officer has a special offer.

Sign away another two to six years of your life and we'll give you ninety-six hours to enjoy a world where death doesn't matter.

The absurdity isn't that soldiers enjoy video games. Millions of civilians do.

It's that an institution entrusted with the power to wage actual war has discovered that four days of virtual lawlessness make an attractive sweetener for years of military obligation.

Four days to play at being a criminal.

Up to six years to serve an institution that can legally order you into situations where people die.

And somewhere in an American military office, somebody is congratulating himself on a successful recruitment strategy.

text:
LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM

MY FAMILY FOUGHT FOR NIGERIA’S INDEPENDENCE AND UNITY. I WILL NOT STAND BY WHILE IT IS DESTROYED.

By Kio Amachree
Political Scientist | President, Worldview International
Stockholm, Sweden — 20 November 2026

I did not suddenly discover patriotism when Bola Ahmed Tinubu became President of Nigeria. Patriotism runs through my family’s history. The struggle for Nigeria’s independence, its survival as a united nation, and the defence of its constitutional institutions are part of my inheritance. And I make absolutely no apologies for it.

My grandfather, Chief Sekin Jaja Amachree, was an elected member of the Eastern House of Assembly and one of the Nigerians who participated in the historic 1958 Constitutional Conference at Lancaster House in London, where the constitutional arrangements leading to Nigeria’s independence were negotiated.

His participation is documented in the original British government report, Command Paper 569, published in November 1958, where he is listed on page 40 as Chief S. J. Amachree, M.H.A., an official adviser to the Action Group delegation.

My grandfather was not merely an observer of Nigerian history. He helped shape it.

His eldest son, my father, Chief Godfrey Kio-Jaja Amachree, QC, went on to serve Nigeria in some of the highest legal and administrative positions in the country. He was Solicitor-General, Acting Attorney-General and Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. He subsequently rose to the rank of Under-Secretary at the United Nations, an extraordinary achievement for an African diplomat of his generation.

These were not men who merely waved flags, shouted slogans or enriched themselves through political connections.

They helped build institutions.

They believed in public service.

They understood that Nigeria was greater than any individual, political party, ethnic group or temporary occupant of public office.

So when supporters of the All Progressives Congress tell me that I am wasting my time writing about Nigeria from Stockholm, I have a very simple answer: You have absolutely no idea who you are talking to, or what my family has contributed to the country you are helping to destroy.

And while I am on the subject, let me address those detractors who continually complain that I write too much about my family, my father, my grandfather and the important men and women whose lives were intertwined with the creation and preservation of Nigeria.

To those people, I have an equally simple message: You can go to hell.

I am part of Nigerian history, whether you like it or not.

My family’s contributions to the independence, development and continued existence of Nigeria are matters of historical record. My personal relationships with the important men who helped create and maintain this country are part of my own life and experiences, and I will not bury them under the carpet simply because certain individuals appear to suffer from serious inferiority complexes.

Why should I apologise for my ancestry?

Why should I conceal my father’s achievements?

Why should I stop speaking about my grandfather’s contribution to independence?

And why should I pretend that I did not grow up surrounded by people who helped shape modern Nigeria?

I am proud of my roots. I am proud of my family. I am proud of my name. And I will never apologise for any of them.

I do not believe that my ancestry makes me superior to another human being. But neither will I diminish my family’s achievements to accommodate the jealousy, ignorance or insecurity of others.

My family history is not a boast. It is part of Nigeria’s national history, and I intend to continue writing about it for as long as I live.

HISTORY DOES NOT STOP AT NATIONAL BORDERS

There is something particularly amusing about people who believe that living abroad disqualifies a citizen from participating in the political destiny of his country.

Have these people ever opened a history book?

Vladimir Lenin was living in Switzerland before travelling through wartime Germany to return to Russia in 1917. He subsequently led the Bolsheviks in overthrowing the Provisional Government.

Fidel Castro organised his return to Cuba from exile in Mexico.

Mao Zedong’s revolutionary career was different, but his movement also demonstrated that political power is not necessarily determined by the location of its opponents.

I am not Lenin, Castro or Mao.

Nor am I advocating an armed revolution.

I am advocating constitutional democracy, honest elections, accountable government and the absolute right of Nigerians to determine who governs them.

But history teaches us something important: political change is not confined to those who happen to be physically present within a country’s borders.

I live in Stockholm. I remain Nigerian by birth, heritage, conviction and responsibility.

And no APC spokesman, political sycophant or government-sponsored propagandist will tell me when I may speak about the country my family helped to build.

MY FATHER FOUGHT TO KEEP NIGERIA UNITED

During the Nigerian Civil War, General Yakubu Gowon turned to my father because of his international standing and the influential relationships he had developed during his years at the United Nations.

My father was appointed a special envoy to the United States, where he used his diplomatic connections to advance the Federal Government’s position, including through contacts within the American establishment and the international oil industry.

His efforts, as recounted in our family’s account of his diplomatic service, contributed to the support and understanding the Federal Government needed during one of the most dangerous periods in Nigeria’s existence.

General Gowon and his government appreciated his contribution.

My father believed Nigeria should remain united.

And he acted on that conviction.

Over the years, I have been subjected to all manner of insults from supporters of Biafran independence because of my father’s role during the war.

I have been called names, attacked personally and accused of defending the wrong side of history.

Let me make something perfectly clear.

I make no apologies whatsoever for my father’s service to Nigeria or his commitment to preserving the federation.

The Civil War was a tragedy that cost an appalling number of lives, and the suffering of the Igbo people must never be dismissed or forgotten. But defending Nigeria’s unity was a legitimate political conviction, just as acknowledging the suffering and grievances that produced the conflict is an essential part of understanding our history.

My father was not solely responsible for preserving Nigeria. No single individual could claim such an achievement.

But he played his part, and I am proud of him.

His diplomatic career and contributions deserve serious historical examination, not the abuse of people who prefer slogans to scholarship.

BUT UNITY CANNOT BECOME AN EXCUSE FOR DICTATORSHIP

For most of my life, I have been an uncompromising believer in the Nigerian union.

My father was Kalabari. My mother was Yoruba. I was born in Lagos. My family history crosses the very ethnic boundaries that politicians continually exploit for personal advantage.

I have argued passionately with my Igbo brothers and sisters against the dismemberment of Nigeria.

But I must now say something that I never imagined I would have to say.

If the 2027 presidential election is rigged to return Bola Ahmed Tinubu to power, and if the courts knowingly legitimise proven electoral fraud, my own commitment to the present constitutional arrangement will be profoundly shaken.

Why should Nigerians be expected to defend a federation if the federation refuses to defend their democratic rights?

Why should citizens continue to accept a political system in which elections become expensive ceremonies designed to legitimise decisions already taken by powerful men?

What is the value of national unity if it means permanent submission to corruption, intimidation and political manipulation?

I do not want Nigeria divided.

I want Nigeria rescued.

But unity must be based on justice, equality, democratic legitimacy and mutual respect.

It cannot be maintained indefinitely through fear, bribery, rigging and the manipulation of ethnic loyalties.

And if those in power believe that the Nigerian people will accept another disputed election without serious resistance through lawful and peaceful means, they may be making a catastrophic political miscalculation.

I WILL NOT ACCEPT ETHNIC DOMINATION DISGUISED AS DEMOCRACY

I am particularly disturbed by the ethnic protectionism surrounding Bola Tinubu.

I have described this tendency as the attempted construction of a Yoruba political dictatorship, and I do not withdraw my criticism of those who place ethnic loyalty above the Constitution.

But let nobody misunderstand me.

I am half Yoruba myself.

I know perfectly well that millions of Yoruba men and women are decent, educated, patriotic Nigerians who do not support corruption or political oppression.

My quarrel is not with the Yoruba people.

My quarrel is with those who believe that because a president belongs to their ethnic group, they must defend him regardless of his conduct.

That is tribalism at its most destructive.

It is the same mentality that has repeatedly prevented Nigeria from developing a genuinely national political culture.

I was born and raised in Lagos.

My maternal grandfather, Chief Ben Oluwole, was a prominent Nigerian banker and a respected figure in Lagos society. Our family home, Kaduna Lodge in Yaba, remains an important part of our history.

My maternal family has deep roots in Lagos and Sagamu.

I can tell you who my father was.

I can tell you who my mother was.

I can tell you about my grandparents, my family history, my education and the institutions in which I have worked.

I have nothing to conceal.

So why should Nigerians be criticised for asking equally searching questions about the background, identity, education and financial history of the man occupying their highest political office?

These are not unreasonable questions.

They are questions of public accountability.

THE TINUBU IDENTITY CONTROVERSY MUST BE SETTLED WITH EVIDENCE

For years, controversies have surrounded Bola Tinubu’s personal history, educational records, earlier identity documents and financial dealings.

Some of the allegations circulating about him remain disputed or unproven. That includes claims about the use of another person’s identity, his family origins and the circumstances surrounding particular travel documents.

But uncertainty is precisely why transparent disclosure matters.

A president should not require an army of lawyers, political loyalists and government spokesmen to answer straightforward questions about his own past.

The 1993 United States civil forfeiture proceedings involving funds associated with Tinubu are a matter of public record. They deserve accurate scrutiny, without confusing a civil settlement with a criminal conviction.

Questions concerning his educational records and the inconsistencies alleged by critics also deserve careful, independent examination.

My intention is to dismantle the political mythology surrounding Bola Tinubu through documents, historical records, credible testimony and verifiable facts.

Not through fabricated stories.

Not through tribal insults.

And certainly not through the worship of a political figure as though he were a monarch or a deity.

If his record is beyond reproach, let the evidence speak.

If serious wrongdoing can be established, let the law take its course.

Nigeria deserves nothing less.

THE PRESIDENT’S CHIEF OF STAFF AND HIS AMERICAN LEGAL RECORD

Now let us examine the man Bola Tinubu appointed as his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Here we are not dealing with political gossip, speculation or allegations invented by opponents.

We are dealing with a documented American Supreme Court disciplinary judgment.

On 26 February 2007, the Supreme Court of Georgia suspended Gbajabiamila from practising law for 36 months.

The case, In the Matter of Femi Gbaja, is reported at 281 Georgia Reports 659.

According to the judgment, Gbajabiamila received $25,000 in settlement of a client’s personal injury claim. The money was deposited into his attorney trust account in January 2003.

The court recorded that he subsequently withdrew the money for his own use, closed his law practice and left the United States.

The client was eventually repaid in 2006.

Gbajabiamila admitted professional misconduct in the disciplinary proceedings. The violations were serious enough to carry the possibility of disbarment, although the court imposed a three-year suspension.

Let that sink in.

The man appointed Chief of Staff to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria had been suspended from practising law in the United States following admitted professional misconduct involving $25,000 belonging to a client.

This was a professional disciplinary case, not a criminal conviction. That distinction must be made clear.

Gbajabiamila subsequently offered a different explanation, claiming that a paralegal employee had taken the money.

But the original American court judgment remains part of the public record.

Reports in 2023 also stated that his Georgia Bar membership had been terminated in 2020.

Now I ask Nigerians a very simple question.

What standards of integrity are being applied when individuals are appointed to the highest offices in our country?

The Chief of Staff to the President is not an insignificant political functionary.

He is one of the most influential people in the executive branch, controlling access to the president and participating in the administration of government.

A lawyer’s responsibility to protect money entrusted to him by a client is fundamental.

If a lawyer breaches that trust, the matter is serious.

And if that lawyer subsequently occupies one of the most powerful administrative positions in Nigeria, the public has every right to scrutinise the circumstances.

I am not suggesting that professional misconduct makes rehabilitation impossible.

I am asking why the Nigerian public should not be entitled to a full explanation of the standards applied when such appointments are made.

The Nigerian presidency should represent the highest standards of public integrity, not the lowest standards that political loyalty can excuse.

LOOK AT THE COMPANY OUR LEADERS KEEP

I am also deeply concerned by the people who have gained influence and access within the present administration.

Gilbert Chagoury, the Lebanese-Nigerian businessman whose name has become associated with major Nigerian infrastructure projects, has a documented history of legal controversy.

His Swiss money-laundering conviction arising from the Abacha era is a matter of public record, as is his later settlement of a United States campaign-finance investigation.

The scale of government contracts involving businesses associated with him raises legitimate questions about procurement transparency, competition and the relationship between private wealth and political influence.

Those questions deserve answers.

What competitive procedures were followed?

Who are the beneficial owners of the companies involved?

How were contract prices determined?

What independent safeguards exist against conflicts of interest?

And why should Nigerians be expected to accept enormous public expenditure without full disclosure?

I also question the standards by which individuals are selected for sensitive positions close to the presidency, particularly when serious professional or disciplinary controversies have surrounded their past conduct.

Public office is not a private club.

The presidency is not a rehabilitation centre for politically connected individuals with questionable records.

The higher the office, the higher the standard of integrity should be. Not the other way around.

RIVERS STATE IS NOT NYESOM WIKE’S PRIVATE ESTATE

Then there is Nyesom Wike.

I have said it before, and I will say it again.

Rivers State is not a feudal estate.

It does not belong to Wike, Tinubu, the APC or any political godfather.

It belongs to the people of Rivers State.

My family helped build that state. My father contributed to its early development, and generations of Kalabari, Ikwerre, Ogoni, Okrika and other Rivers communities have invested their lives and futures in it.

No politician has the right to treat its institutions as personal property.

I reject the culture of political intimidation, patronage and domination that has come to characterise so much of Nigerian politics.

And I particularly reject the suggestion that political power confers some hereditary entitlement to control a state long after leaving office.

Wike is a public servant and politician.

Nothing more.

He is not a king.

He is not a feudal lord.

And he is certainly not the owner of Rivers State.

WHAT EXAMPLE ARE WE SETTING FOR OUR CHILDREN?

This is perhaps what angers me most.

What are young Nigerians supposed to learn from the conduct of their political leaders?

That education is less important than political connections?

That honesty is a disadvantage?

That the quickest route to wealth is through public office?

That bribery, intimidation, deceit and ethnic favouritism are acceptable instruments of political success?

That the police and security services exist to protect powerful individuals rather than the Constitution?

What kind of country are we creating?

Nigeria has extraordinary human talent.

We have brilliant scientists, lawyers, doctors, engineers, entrepreneurs, academics, musicians and young innovators.

Yet millions of our citizens struggle to obtain electricity, medical care, employment, education and basic security.

Meanwhile, political elites compete over access to public money, contracts, official privileges and personal influence.

A nation cannot become great by rewarding dishonesty and punishing integrity.

It cannot become prosperous when public institutions are captured by private interests.

And it cannot become united when politicians continually exploit ethnic divisions to escape accountability.

TO THOSE WHO SAY I AM WASTING MY TIME

I have heard the insults.

I have heard the mockery.

I have heard the suggestion that because I live in Sweden, I should keep quiet about Nigeria.

My answer remains unchanged.

My grandfather helped advance the cause of independence.

My father served the Nigerian state and represented its interests internationally during a war that threatened its existence.

And I have inherited their belief that public service is a responsibility, not an opportunity for personal enrichment.

I do not need an appointment from Bola Tinubu.

I do not need a government contract.

I do not need a political patron.

I do not need to belong to the APC, the PDP or any other political organisation to exercise my constitutional right to criticise those who govern my country.

And I certainly do not need permission from a political sycophant to defend the principles my family stood for.

I write because I believe Nigeria is worth saving.

I write because I refuse to accept that corruption is our national destiny.

I write because the millions of Nigerians suffering under insecurity, unemployment, poverty and institutional failure deserve better.

And I write because silence in the face of serious injustice is not neutrality.

It is surrender.

MY FINAL WARNING: NIGERIA BELONGS TO NIGERIANS

Let the message be understood in Abuja, Lagos, Port Harcourt and every corner of the federation.

The 2027 elections must be free, fair, transparent and credible.

There must be no rigging.

No intimidation of voters.

No manipulation of results.

No abuse of the police, military or intelligence services for partisan purposes.

No judicial endorsement of proven electoral fraud.

And no attempt to transform the Nigerian presidency into the personal property of one man, one family, one ethnic group or one political organisation.

I am not advocating violence.

I am advocating something far more powerful and enduring: the organised, determined and peaceful exercise of the sovereignty of the Nigerian people.

The Constitution belongs to the people.

The armed forces swear allegiance to the Constitution, not to Bola Tinubu.

The police exist to protect citizens, not to terrorise political opponents.

The courts exist to administer justice, not to manufacture legitimacy for those in power.

And the presidency is a temporary public trust, not a throne.

I have defended Nigeria’s unity throughout my life.

But I will not defend a union emptied of democracy, justice and equal citizenship.

My loyalty is to Nigeria, not to Tinubu.

My loyalty is to the Constitution, not to the APC.

My loyalty is to the Nigerian people, not to the political class that has so often betrayed them.

My grandfather’s generation fought for independence.

My father’s generation fought to preserve the federation.

My generation must now fight, through every legitimate democratic and constitutional means available, to ensure that the country they helped build is not reduced to a private enterprise for the politically connected.

That is my inheritance.

That is my responsibility.

And that is why I will continue to speak.

God is watching.

The soul of Nigeria is hurting.

And those who believe they can continue humiliating, exploiting and deceiving the Nigerian people indefinitely should remember one fundamental truth:

No president is greater than the nation. No political party is greater than the people. And no amount of money, propaganda, intimidation or electoral manipulation can confer moral legitimacy on a government that has lost the trust of its citizens.

I will not be silenced.

I will not be intimidated.

And I will not apologise for defending my country.

My family helped build Nigeria. I refuse to stand by and watch it being destroyed.

I am proud of my roots. I am proud of my family. I am proud of my name. And to those who cannot accept that, I make absolutely no apologies.

I rest my case.

Kio Amachree
Political Scientist
President, Worldview International

text:
Last year, China saw a boom in foundation models, the do-everything large language models that underpin the AI revolution. This year, the focus has shifted to AI agents—systems that are less about responding to users’ queries and more about autonomously accomplishing things for them. 

There are now a host of Chinese startups building these general-purpose digital tools, which can answer emails, browse the internet to plan vacations, and even design an interactive website. Many of these have emerged in just the last two months, following in the footsteps of Manus—a general AI agent that sparked weeks of social media frenzy for invite codes after its limited-release launch in early March. 

These emerging AI agents aren’t large language models themselves. Instead, they’re built on top of them, using a workflow-based structure designed to get things done. A lot of these systems also introduce a different way of interacting with AI. Rather than just chatting back and forth with users, they are optimized for managing and executing multistep tasks—booking flights, managing schedules, conducting research—by using external tools and remembering instructions. 

China could take the lead on building these kinds of agents. The country’s tightly integrated app ecosystems, rapid product cycles, and digitally fluent user base could provide a favorable environment for embedding AI into daily life. 

For now, its leading AI agent startups are focusing their attention on the global market, because the best Western models don’t operate inside China’s firewalls. But that could change soon: Tech giants like ByteDance and Tencent are preparing their own AI agents that could bake automation directly into their native super-apps, pulling data from their vast ecosystem of programs that dominate many aspects of daily life in the country. 

As the race to define what a useful AI agent looks like unfolds, a mix of ambitious startups and entrenched tech giants are now testing how these tools might actually work in practice—and for whom.

Set the standard

It’s been a whirlwind few months for Manus, which was developed by the startup Butterfly Effect. The company raised $75 million in a funding round led by the US venture capital firm Benchmark, took the product on an ambitious global roadshow, and hired dozens of new employees. 

Even before registration opened to the public in May, Manus had become a reference point for what a broad, consumer‑oriented AI agent should accomplish. Rather than handling narrow chores for businesses, this “general” agent is designed to be able to help with everyday tasks like trip planning, stock comparison, or your kid’s school project. 

Unlike previous AI agents, Manus uses a browser-based sandbox that lets users supervise the agent like an intern, watching in real time as it scrolls through web pages, reads articles, or codes actions. It also proactively asks clarifying questions, supports long-term memory that would serve as context for future tasks.

“Manus represents a promising product experience for AI agents,” says Ang Li, cofounder and CEO of Simular, a startup based in Palo Alto, California, that’s building AI agents that operate a real computer. “I believe Chinese startups have a huge advantage when it comes to designing consumer products, thanks to cutthroat domestic competition that leads to fast execution and greater attention to product details.”

In the case of Manus, the competition is moving fast. Two of the most buzzy follow‑ups, Genspark and Flowith, for example, are already boasting benchmark scores that match or edge past Manus’s. 

Genspark, led by former Baidu executives Eric Jing and Kay Zhu, links many small “super agents” through what it calls multi‑component prompting. The agent can switch among several large language models, accepts both images and text, and carries out tasks from making slide decks to placing phone calls. Whereas Manus relies heavily on Browser Use, a popular open-source product that lets agents operate a web browser in a virtual window like a human, Genspark directly integrates with a wide array of tools and APIs. Launched in April, the company says that it already has over 5 million users and over $36 million in yearly revenue.

Flowith, the work of a young team that first grabbed public attention in April 2025 at a developer event hosted by the popular social media app Xiaohongshu, takes a different tack. Marketed as an “infinite agent,” it opens on a blank canvas where each question becomes a node on a branching map. Users can backtrack, take new branches, and store results in personal or sharable “knowledge gardens”—a design that feels more like project management software (think Notion) than a typical chat interface. Every inquiry or task builds its own mind-map-like graph, encouraging a more nonlinear and creative interaction with AI. Flowith’s core agent, NEO, runs in the cloud and can perform scheduled tasks like sending emails and compiling files. The founders want the app to be a “knowledge marketbase”, and aims to tap into the social aspect of AI with the aspiration of becoming “the OnlyFans of AI knowledge creators”.

What they also share with Manus is the global ambition. Both Genspark and Flowith have stated that their primary focus is the international market.

A global address

Startups like Manus, Genspark, and Flowith—though founded by Chinese entrepreneurs—could blend seamlessly into the global tech scene and compete effectively abroad. Founders, investors, and analysts that MIT Technology Review has spoken to believe Chinese companies are moving fast, executing well, and quickly coming up with new products. 

Money reinforces the pull to launch overseas. Customers there pay more, and there are plenty to go around. “You can price in USD, and with the exchange rate that’s a sevenfold multiplier,” Manus cofounder Xiao Hong quipped on a podcast. “Even if we’re only operating at 10% power because of cultural differences overseas, we’ll still make more than in China.”

But creating the same functionality in China is a challenge. Major US AI companies including OpenAI and Anthropic have opted out of mainland China because of geopolitical risks and challenges with regulatory compliance. Their absence initially created a black market as users resorted to VPNs and third-party mirrors to access tools like ChatGPT and Claude. That vacuum has since been filled by a new wave of Chinese chatbots—DeepSeek, Doubao, Kimi—but the appetite for foreign models hasn’t gone away. 

Manus, for example, uses Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet—widely considered the top model for agentic tasks. Manus cofounder Zhang Tao has repeatedly praised Claude’s ability to juggle tools, remember contexts, and hold multi‑round conversations—all crucial for turning chatty software into an effective executive assistant.

But the company’s use of Sonnet has made its agent functionally unusable inside China without a VPN. If you open Manus from a mainland IP address, you’ll see a notice explaining that the team is “working on integrating Qwen’s model,” a special local version that is built on top of Alibaba’s open-source model. 

An engineer overseeing ByteDance’s work on developing an agent, who spoke to MIT Technology Review anonymously to avoid sanction, said that the absence of Claude Sonnet models “limits everything we do in China.” DeepSeek’s open models, he added, still hallucinate too often and lack training on real‑world workflows. Developers we spoke with rank Alibaba’s Qwen series as the best domestic alternative, yet most say that switching to Qwen knocks performance down a notch.

Jiaxin Pei, a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford’s Institute for Human‑Centered AI, thinks that gap will close: “Building agentic capabilities in base LLMs has become a key focus for many LLM builders, and once people realize the value of this, it will only be a matter of time.”

For now, Manus is doubling down on audiences it can already serve. In a written response, the company said its “primary focus is overseas expansion,” noting that new offices in San Francisco, Singapore, and Tokyo have opened in the past month.

A super‑app approach

Although the concept of AI agents is still relatively new, the consumer-facing AI app market in China is already crowded with major tech players. DeepSeek remains the most widely used, while ByteDance’s Doubao and Moonshot’s Kimi have also become household names. However, most of these apps are still optimized for chat and entertainment rather than task execution. This gap in the local market has pushed China’s big tech firms to roll out their own user-facing agents, though early versions remain uneven in quality and rough around the edges. 

ByteDance is testing Coze Space, an AI agent based on its own Doubao model family that lets users toggle between “plan” and “execute” modes, so they can either directly guide the agent’s actions or step back and watch it work autonomously. It connects up to 14 popular apps, including GitHub, Notion, and the company’s own Lark office suite. Early reviews say the tool can feel clunky and has a high failure rate, but it clearly aims to match what Manus offers.

Meanwhile, Zhipu AI has released a free agent called AutoGLM Rumination, built on its proprietary ChatGLM models. Shanghai‑based Minimax has launched Minimax Agent. Both products look almost identical to Manus and demo basic tasks such as building a simple website, planning a trip, making a small Flash game, or running quick data analysis.

Despite the limited usability of most general AI agents launched within China, big companies have plans to change that. During a May 15 earnings call, Tencent president Liu Zhiping teased an agent that would weave automation directly into China’s most ubiquitous app, WeChat. 

Considered the original super-app, WeChat already handles messaging, mobile payments, news, and millions of mini‑programs that act like embedded apps. These programs give Tencent, its developer, access to data from millions of services that pervade everyday life in China, an advantage most competitors can only envy.

Historically, China’s consumer internet has splintered into competing walled gardens—share a Taobao link in WeChat and it resolves as plaintext, not a preview card. Unlike the more interoperable Western internet, China’s tech giants have long resisted integration with one another, choosing to wage platform war at the expense of a seamless user experience.

But the use of mini‑programs has given WeChat unprecedented reach across services that once resisted interoperability, from gym bookings to grocery orders. An agent able to roam that ecosystem could bypass the integration headaches dogging independent startups.

Alibaba, the e-commerce giant behind the Qwen model series, has been a front-runner in China’s AI race but has been slower to release consumer-facing products. Even though Qwen was the most downloaded open-source model on Hugging Face in 2024, it didn’t power a dedicated chatbot app until early 2025. In March, Alibaba rebranded its cloud storage and search app Quark into an all-in-one AI search tool. By June, Quark had introduced DeepResearch—a new mode that marks its most agent-like effort to date. 

ByteDance and Alibaba did not reply to MIT Technology Review’s request for comments.

“Historically, Chinese tech products tend to pursue the all-in-one, super-app approach, and the latest Chinese AI agents reflect just that,” says Li of Simular, who previously worked at Google DeepMind on lifelong learning agents. “In contrast, AI agents in the US are more focused on serving specific verticals.”

Pei, the researcher at Stanford, says that existing tech giants could have a huge advantage in bringing the vision of general AI agents to life—especially those with built-in integration across services. “The customer-facing AI agent market is still very early, with tons of problems like authentication and liability,” he says. “But companies that already operate across a wide range of services have a natural advantage in deploying agents at scale.”

The Philippines is back in the international rice market following a partial rollback of import restrictions, reviving demand for Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar just as exportable supplies tighten across Southeast Asia.

ASIAN RICE FOB PRICES (USD/MT)

• Thailand 25% broken white: $472.
• Myanmar 25% broken white: $458.
• India 25% broken white: $389.
• Pakistan 25% broken white: $389.

India and Pakistan are offering a $69/MT discount to Myanmar, $83 to Thailand and a massive $170 to Vietnamese fragrant rice.

VIETNAM: PREMIUM PRICES, TIGHT SUPPLIES

• Vietnamese DT8 fragrant 25% broken rice is being discussed at around $550/MT FOB.
• Shipment: December 2026.
• Parcel size: 5,000 MT.
• Nearby export availability is expected to remain limited through February 2027.

PHILIPPINES: IMPORT DEMAND RETURNS

Earlier restrictions included:
• July suspension of 5% broken white rice imports.
• September suspension of sanitary and phytosanitary clearances for shipments from Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar.
• Imports of 15–25% broken rice have now resumed.

Some trade channels reportedly face quota ceilings of around 300,000 MT through February, although the extent of these restrictions remains disputed.

THE BIG MARKET DEVELOPMENT

Vietnam and Thailand are benefiting from renewed Philippine demand, but their elevated prices are creating opportunities for India and Pakistan.

If Vietnamese offers continue climbing, Philippine buyers could increasingly switch towards cheaper South Asian origins.

MARKET OUTLOOK

• Vietnam: Slightly firmer.
• Thailand: Firm to slightly higher.
• Myanmar: Supported by renewed regional demand.
• India and Pakistan: Competitive advantage in lower-priced broken rice.

EL NIÑO RISK: A strong El Niño is expected to persist into the first half of 2027, raising concerns over moisture availability and upcoming rice production across parts of Asia.

My takeaway: Philippine buying is providing fresh bullish momentum to Asian rice prices, but the $170/MT price gap between Vietnamese fragrant rice and Indian/Pakistani 25% broken rice is too significant to ignore.

India and Pakistan could capture a larger share of price-sensitive Philippine demand if Southeast Asian export offers become increasingly expensive.

text:
THE ECB SEES SUBPRIME IN HOW AI IS FINANCED, DOTCOM IN WHAT IS BUILT.

On Nov 18, 2026, the European Central Bank published its Financial Stability Review. Box 3 covers how the AI build gets financed. Its conclusion opens with this line:

"The rapid shift towards debt finance invokes historical parallels with the dotcom and subprime bubbles"

The ECB ties the subprime comparison to how the money moves: circular financing, off-balance-sheet deals and opaque private markets. Three findings from the box stand out.

First, commitments that are not on the balance sheet. Hyperscalers sign long leases and purchase contracts, and data center developers and chip owners borrow against those payments. The ECB puts the off-balance-sheet commitments of big tech firms, Nvidia, Oracle and Anthropic included, at more than $4 trillion as of Q2 2026, well above their on-balance-sheet liabilities.

"Such cash flow commitments are debt-like in economic terms, but they do not appear as liabilities on the balance sheets of hyperscalers under US accounting standards"

Second, demand that is partly self-financed. Chipmakers often finance the chip purchases of their own customers. The ECB says this inflates the expected revenues of both sides.

Third, long debt against short-lived chips. Per the ECB's chart notes, market intelligence puts the economic life of AI equipment at 1 to 3 years. The same notes say most hyperscalers raised the accounting life of servers from 3 years in 2020 to 6 years in 2026.

"the maturity of hyperscalers' outstanding debt exceeds the economic lifetimes of a substantial share of the physical capital funded by this debt"

Two facts keep this in proportion. The Fed's Nov 13, 2026 report notes that such commitments are generally undiscounted, so they are not directly comparable with balance sheet debt. And the broad measure of euro area bank lending to AI-related sectors is about €75 billion, 1.1% of their committed corporate exposures. The ECB says this broad measure overestimates the exposure.

The ECB sees the bigger exposure in non-banks: funds, insurers and pension funds. As of Q2 2026, US tech and AI-related firms made up 16% to 26% of the equity investments of euro area non-banks.

The dotcom bust, the ECB writes, brought "only a shallow recession thanks to a large share of equity finance."

My read:

The question is not whether AI works. The ECB says even a successful AI build may end in "overcapacity, capital misallocation and credit losses for investors" if it runs on debt.

The warning is conditional. The same box says: "So far, however, hyperscalers' earnings have broadly kept up with expectations."

What would change my mind: hyperscaler free cash flow turning positive sooner than the ECB expects (for most hyperscalers it expects it to stay negative until 2028), and spreads on hyperscaler bonds falling back toward those of equally rated companies.

Three lines in the hyperscaler filings show whether the debt is running ahead of the revenue: leases signed but not yet commenced, purchase obligations, and the useful life of servers. The first two are mostly in the quarterly 10-Q notes, the third in the annual 10-K notes.

QUASAR MARKETS · DAILY MARKET BRIEFING

Friday, November 20, 2026 · What to think about today

THE BIG PICTURE

The two engines that powered this bull market are reversing at the same time. Cheap money is gone, because the Federal Reserve now looks set to raise rates again in December as inflation worries mount, and the AI trade, the market’s other growth engine, is unwinding fast after Anthropic’s record IPO failed to reignite the fervor. As a result, stocks just logged a sixth straight down day, the longest losing streak since 2024. So here is the question for today: is this a healthy reset, or the first leg of something deeper?

The AI trade cracks even as Anthropic’s IPO soars

AI and Tech · $NVDA 

Anthropic went public Thursday in a record IPO and popped roughly 17% from its $83 offer price, yet the broader AI complex still sank. Meanwhile Nvidia fell for a sixth straight session and is now down about 27% in a month, its worst run since 2008, even after posting $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue. In other words, blowout fundamentals no longer earn a stock a bid, which is exactly what late-cycle unwinds look like. For the running tape on the complex, see the Quasar Markets AI Tracker.

What to watch: whether buyers defend Nvidia’s post-earnings lows, or let the selling feed on itself.

The Fed is tightening into the sell-off

Fed · $TLT

Markets have flipped hard, from pricing rate cuts to pricing hikes. Traders now see better than a 90% chance the Fed raises rates on December 9, and money markets price at least two more hikes by mid-2027 as inflation refuses to cool. Consequently, the old “bad news is good news” cushion is gone, because a weak tape no longer pulls forward any rate relief. Track the moves on the Quasar Markets Rates Desk.

The tension: every hot data point now tightens financial conditions instead of loosening them.

Bitcoin breaks as risk appetite vanishes

Crypto · $BTC

Bitcoin slid below $62,000, its lowest level since July, while more than $528 million in leveraged positions were liquidated overnight. Furthermore, crypto’s Fear and Greed gauge has collapsed to 10, deep in extreme fear, and chart watchers are flagging a possible death cross. Because crypto trades as the market’s highest-beta risk asset, it tends to break first and hardest whenever liquidity tightens. Follow the tape on the Quasar Markets Crypto Desk.

What to watch: whether Bitcoin holds the July lows, or opens a fresh leg lower.

A rising dollar exports the pain worldwide

Global · $DXY

The sell-off went global overnight. Japan’s Nikkei dropped nearly 5% and South Korea’s Kospi fell 5.2% as the AI rout spread across Asia, while a surging US dollar hit a multi-month high and pushed the euro to a 19-month low. Moreover, the yen weakened to about 159 per dollar, which means the dollar is now the tightening force for everyone else. See the full picture on the Quasar Markets Global Dashboard.

The tension: a stronger dollar tightens conditions everywhere, just as central banks turn hawkish.

THE QUESTION FOR YOU

Is this the AI bubble finally deflating, or just a healthy reset after a historic run? And with the Fed leaning toward another hike, what is the one chart you are watching into next week? Drop your take and tell us what you are tracking. $ANT

Central Bank Deputy Governor to Grace Spires5aside Finale in Lagos

The Deputy Governor of Corporate Services of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Dr. Muhammad Sani Abdullahi, PhD, will lead a list of high-profile dignitaries to the grand finale of the 2026 Spires5aside Naija Street Soccer Tournament in Lagos this weekend.

The widely respected economic and financial expert, before his appointment by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in September 2023, served as a policy adviser at the Executive Office of former United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon in New York. Dattijo, as he is popularly known, was part of the core team involved in developing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Dr. Muhammad confirmed his attendance during a conversation with the tournament initiator and CEO of Spires Media, Dr. Bankole Allibay, on Tuesday.

Dattijo expressed excitement about attending the third edition of the Spires5aside finale, commending the initiative for empowering young people through sports and technology over the years.

In his words:

“The Spires 5-Aside project is another medium to propel our youth in sports. The next generation of footballers must have a platform to hone their skills, and this is what the organisers have created.”

Dr. Muhammad also commended the initiator, Dr. Bankole Allibay, for his passion and commitment to youth development, stressing the need to encourage individuals making meaningful contributions to the advancement of Nigerian youths.

“Individuals like Dr. Allibay should be encouraged to do more for the advancement of Nigerian youth. His passion to empower the younger generation should be commended,” the CBN Deputy Governor added.

The grand finale of the annual Spires5aside Naija Street Soccer Tournament 2026 is scheduled to hold on Saturday, November 14, at the Union Bank Sports Ground, off Bode Thomas Street, Surulere, Lagos.

Sixteen qualified teams from the five divisions of Lagos State began their campaign on Tuesday, October 27, competing for glory in this year’s championship.

Over ₦10 million in prize money, alongside various team and individual awards, will be presented at the grand finale.

As part of the closing ceremony, Spires Media, in partnership with telecommunications infrastructure giant IHS Nigeria, will also present 52 free laptops to selected participants of the Spires Sport Meet Tech programme. The initiative recently concluded in Lagos, where over 200 young people received training in modern digital skills, including Microsoft applications, coding, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and other technology fields.

The 2026 finale promises to be a celebration of football, youth empowerment, technology, and community development, reinforcing the vision of Spires5aside to build minds and inspire futures.

Everyone in crypto loves talking about the "RWA decade," but most of the time it just sounds like empty buzzwords.

If you actually scroll through what @redstone_defi has been shipping lately, you can see what real institutional adoption looks like behind the scenes.

They just turned 6 years old, and their mission to build the infrastructure for the next era of finance is starting to click into place. Here is everything they have been putting together recently:

1. A seat at Wall Street's table
RedStone just joined the DTC Digital Assets Solutions Industry Working Group (IWG), convened by @The_DTCC. The group focuses on discussion, feedback, and alignment around the DTCC Tokenization Service. Getting invited into that room is a massive signal that traditional finance is taking onchain infrastructure seriously.

2. Solving the privacy problem banks actually care about
Back in 2024, one of Wall Street's largest banks had to pay $249M after its block desk tipped off investors about clients' upcoming share sales. Onchain, a similar leak can happen through the oracle itself, because a push feed can see who is reading which price and when. To close that gap, RedStone built CAPS on @CantonNetwork to bring private pricing onchain, giving everyone one official price without leaking trading activity.

3. Pricing stocks when Wall Street is asleep
Traditional markets close, but global news does not. With seven tokenized NVIDIA stocks facing three off-hour market shocks, how do onchain markets price NVDA when Wall Street is shut? @MarcinRedStone and @bvicentes from @CredoraNetwork broke this down in a deep dive hosted by @DefiantNews .

4. Putting idle tokenized stocks to work
As @0xterry2016, co-founder of @lista_dao, pointed out, most tokenized stock supply just sits idle because the lending side was never built around it. Lista DAO took the opposite route by listing wide and fast, supporting nearly every new bStock as collateral from day one across more than 74 pairs today. Because of that, borrowing against tokenized equities on Lista has grown all year even while the rest of the market stalled.
5. The numbers are already getting huge

Standard Chartered projects tokenized RWAs could hit $2T by the end of 2028, driven mostly by funds and equities. You can already see that shape forming:
Spiko's eurSAFO (a tokenized share class of Amundi's SAFO fund) on @StellarOrg launched in March with $100M committed and has already grown to $1.36B. It has 10,456 holders with a median holding of around $17.8K and no single wallet holding over 5%.

Allfunds, a $2T+ institutional fund distribution platform, just selected five @centrifuge powered funds to join its network.

6. Pushing the conversation globally
Beyond the tech, they are actively bridging the gap with builders and banks. On Season 2 Episode 2 of the RedStone Podcast, @mkmassari sat down with Dan Sun, Head of APAC at @Alchemy, to talk about what Asia's banks need before building onchain and why stablecoins matter most for cross-border payments. They are also gearing up for @TokenizeThisNYC 2027 at The Glasshouse, bringing together the people actually moving institutional capital onchain.

Six years in, @redstone_defi is not chasing short-term hype. They are quietly building the data, privacy, and pricing layer that traditional finance actually needs to move onchain.

If you are watching the RWA space, keep a close eye on what they are doing.

⚡ SNF STOCK PULSE™

UTILITIES & POWER INFRASTRUCTURE

FIRSTENERGY ADDS $2 BILLION TO ITS INVESTMENT PLAN. A NEW POWER PLANT APPROVAL CHANGES ITS EARNINGS OUTLOOK.

$FE is expanding its five-year capital program following a consequential regulatory decision in West Virginia.

The development is about more than constructing additional electricity generation.

It changes the company's projected investment base, earnings growth and financing requirements.

WHAT CHANGED

FirstEnergy disclosed Friday that it is increasing its 2026 through 2030 Energize365 investment program from $36 billion to $38 billion.

Management also raised its long-term non-GAAP Core EPS growth target.

Previous outlook: 6% to 8% annual growth.

New outlook: 7% to 9%, targeting the upper half of that range.

The catalyst is a November 17 order from the West Virginia Public Service Commission.

Regulators approved a certificate authorizing FirstEnergy subsidiaries to construct the Maidsville Energy Center, a planned 1,200 MW combined-cycle natural gas facility.

The order also authorizes a surcharge designed to recover financing costs during construction.

That provision matters.

Large generation investments require substantial capital well before they begin producing electricity.

Regulatory mechanisms allowing cost recovery during construction can help reduce financing pressure and improve investment economics.

But there’s a second side to this announcement.

FirstEnergy expects to fund approximately 35% of Maidsville's capital investment through equity or equity-like securities.

Its anticipated equity financing requirement for 2026 through 2030 is increasing from $2 billion to $2.8 billion.

Higher projected earnings growth therefore comes with greater capital requirements.

WHAT SNF IS WATCHING

Whether the approved project delivers its expected contribution to regulated earnings without excessive construction costs or financing pressure.

FirstEnergy's expansion also reflects a broader shift in electricity infrastructure investment.

Utilities must support growing demand, improve system reliability and secure adequate generation capacity.

Data centers and industrial electrification may contribute to future load growth.

But potential electricity demand is not the same as a signed customer commitment.

For FirstEnergy, the key confirmations will be project execution, financing terms, construction milestones and the actual recovery of investment costs through regulated mechanisms.

The distinction between rate base growth and shareholder earnings growth is especially important.

More capital investment can expand regulated assets.

But achieving attractive returns depends on approved recovery, execution discipline and the cost of funding that investment.

SNF LENS™

🟢 SIGNAL: A regulatory approval supports an additional $2 billion of planned investment and a higher long term Core EPS growth range.

⚪ NOISE: A larger capital program is not automatically a larger economic return. Electricity demand expectations are not guaranteed customer revenue.

🟡 CONFIRMATION: Maidsville construction progress, effective financing-cost recovery, disciplined spending and delivery of 7% to 9% annual Core EPS growth.

🔴 RISK: Construction delays, equipment costs, interest rates, additional equity requirements, regulatory changes and potential dilution.

BOTTOM LINE

FirstEnergy is demonstrating how new power generation can translate into a larger regulated investment opportunity.

The approval improves visibility for a major capital project and supports management's higher earnings growth ambition.

But the financial outcome still depends on execution.

The company must invest more capital, finance the project and earn sufficient regulated returns to justify the expansion.

The opportunity is now better defined.

The return on that opportunity still has to be earned.

text:
ENGLAND & EU

Hotairman Burnham heads to Brussels as England and EU close in on Brexit reset deal

The last night tensions at the ambassadors meeting will be a sharp lesson for anyone in the UK who clings to the idea that negotiating with the EU comes from a position of strength: the UK is not a member of the EU and despite the warm feelings to the Labour government in European capitals, benefits of the club are not extended to non members.

It also underlines the feeling expressed by several large member states this week that the way forward after this summit is not more iterative reset summits or mini-deals.

Yes, there will be negotiations on allowing the UK into the energy single market as this is in the joint interests of both sides in the wake of the Ukraine war. But no talks on pharma or chemicals, according to some capitals.

As one diplomat said:

“It puts down a marker warning the UK that cherry picking bits of the single market mean you are a rule taker.”

“It makes the choice for Britain starker and more binary” and shows that “the alternatives are basically muddling along with a version of the status quo or rejoining,” they said.

A draft of a joint statement expected to be signed by Andy Burnham and Ursula von der Leyen at a summit on Friday morning states that both sides will establish “a structured dialogue” to discuss “returns to third countries”.

Until now, the Home Office has been seeking bilateral agreements with third countries allowing the removal of migrants, but with no obvious success.

Last week, five EU countries – Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands – announced an agreement in principle with Rwanda to establish a migrant “return hub” there in 2027.

Burnham hinted at possible cooperation with EU countries last week when he told reporters that the 'UK' (Scotland is excluded from talks) had not had direct discussions with European governments involved in return hubs but “we will watch that [the five-country deal] with interest, learning from what went on in the past”. He said: “The public want us to do whatever we can to deal with illegal immigration.”

England has been fighting for deeper cooperation with the EU on migration, with the new deal on a “strategic dialogue” secured in the last two weeks by negotiators in Brussels.

It is a key part of the UK-EU reset pact, which also covers a youth mobility scheme, tariffs on Chinese imports, food and drink exports to the EU and a wider restatement of commitment on defence and security.

Informed sources confirmed this was the first time the EU had agreed to “open a dialogue on returns” after the launch of the bloc’s Channel action plan in June this year.

Whitehall sources said the 'UK' was now open to the possibility of sending rejected claimants to Rwanda – a recent pivot from the position under Starmer’s government, which rejected the move. This is sure to upset Labour's backbenchers.
